jobs.title: Engineering Manager - Akamai Inference Cloud (Remote/Poland)
jobs.excerpt: Are you passionate about building and leading teams that deliver cloud infrastructure at global scale?
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about building and leading teams that deliver cloud infrastructure at global scale?

Do you want to guide a platform engineering team working at the forefront of AI infrastructure?

Join the Akamai Inference Cloud Team!

The Akamai Inference Cloud team is part of Akamai's Cloud Technology Group. We design and operate AI platforms enabling customers to run inference models with unmatched performance, compliance, and economics. We build the foundational infrastructure powering our globally distributed platform - Kubernetes orchestration, GPU resource management, networking, and multi-region deployment.

Partner with the best

As an Engineering Manager, you will lead a team building core infrastructure for large-scale AI inference. You'll drive technical execution, people development, and delivery across Kubernetes orchestration, networking, data plane APIs, and observability. You'll develop a deep understanding of AI infrastructure while guiding your team in building systems serving inference workloads globally.

As an Engineering Manager, you will be responsible for:

  • Leading, mentoring, and growing a team of software engineers and SDETs delivering cloud platform infrastructure across multiple focus areas.
  • Driving technical execution and delivery of Kubernetes orchestration, networking, and platform services on a quarterly roadmap cadence
  • Collaborating with product management, architecture, and peer engineering teams to define priorities, scope work, and manage dependencies across the inference platform.
  • Establishing engineering best practices including code review standards, CI/CD processes, incident response procedures, and observability practices
  • Managing team staffing, hiring, and onboarding to build a high-performing distributed engineering team.
  • Fostering a culture of technical excellence, continuous improvement, and knowledge sharing within the team

Do what you love

To be successful in this role you will:

  • Bring 5 years of experience in software infrastructure development, management, or platform engineering
  • Bring 2+ years managing software engineering teams with experience in hiring, mentoring, and performance feedback
  • Demonstrate technical depth in distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes, or platform engineering practices
  • Show experience managing teams delivering Kubernetes-based infrastructure, networking services, or cloud-native platforms at scale
  • Have proven ability to drive execution across multiple workstreams while balancing technical debt, reliability, and feature delivery
  • Demonstrate communication skills to align technical and business stakeholders across a distributed, multi-timezone organization

About us

At Akamai, we make life better for billions of people, trillions of times a day.
Whether you're streaming live events, scrolling social media, watching your favorite series, or managing your savings, we're the engine behind the scenes. We provide the world's most distributed platform from Cloud to Edge to help the giants of the digital world work faster and stay more secure, making the internet a better experience for everyone.

Our focus is simple:

Cloud and Edge: Running apps closer to users for instant performance.
Security: Neutralizing threats before they ever reach your data.
Content Delivery: Scaling the world's biggest moments without a glitch.
AI: Enabling our customers to build, secure, and scale AI apps on the world's most distributed cloud platform.

At Akamai, we don't just support the internet; we power and protect it, because behind every great digital experience is a massive hidden challenge. And we're the ones who solve it. When millions of people hit play or pay, Akamai ensures it just works.

Benefits at Akamai: We support your health, well-being, finances, and life beyond work. See our benefits.

FlexBase adapts to your job's needs

Akamai's FlexBase program is yet another way we show our commitment to providing employees with an exceptional workplace experience. It's not about telling employees where to work; it's about supporting employees to do their best work.

We trust our incredible employees to work in ways that suit them best: at home, in an office, or a combination of both.

Connect with us on social and see what life at Akamai is like!

At TE, you will unleash your potential working with people from diverse backgrounds and industries to create a safer, sustainable and more connected world.

​

Job Overview

TE's Enterprise Risk & Security Management (ERSM) group is comprised of region-based and enterprise professionals who partner with businesses and functions to protect TE's people, productivity, and profitability around the world. We help the organization win in our markets by delivering outstanding customer service through innovative, risk-based insights and leveraging deep subject matter expertise and experience in Business Continuity, Crisis Management, Enterprise Risk Management, and Physical Security. ERSM's dedicated professionals focus on ensuring TE is proactively managing the dynamic landscape of risks to the organization.

The successful candidate will be able to navigate and thrive in a global environment while maintaining integrity, taking accountability, promoting teamwork and inclusion, and championing innovation. We are a workplace where all voices are heard, valued, and respected, and we welcome talented individuals from every background to join us in making a meaningful impact today.

Role Overview:

The Manager, Resilience Programs, is responsible for managing Business Continuity and Crisis Management programs across the organization through the administration, maintenance, and training of appropriate risk-based, business-focused resilience programs. This role focuses on field applications of TE’s Business Continuity and Crisis Management programs, providing direct support across regions to include program maintenance, training, and communication.   • Conduct periodic compliance and quality audits on TE's business continuity and crisis management programs.
  • Partner with the security & resilience PMO on technology.
  • Work with the ERSM team resilience awareness program, including designing, development, and delivery of training and communication initiatives to ERSM team members, internal stakeholders, and virtually across the globe.

  • Travel – 50% of the time, sometimes on short notice.

  • Must be an expert in business applications of business continuity and crisis management programs.

  • Strong E.I (Emotional Intelligence Index) with exceptional interpersonal skills, communication abilities, and active listening capabilities.
  • Must have Learning & Development best practices knowledge.
  • Must excel at presenting to others and have experience living in different countries.

Your start in the Commercial Excellence & Activation Team ESN & More!

As (Senior) Media & Shopper Activation Manager Drugstore (gn), you are responsible for shopper marketing activations and retail media campaigns with our drugstore partners in Germany and Austria. You bring experience in trade or shopper marketing and want to drive the brands ESN & More Nutrition at the point of sale? Then get in touch and join the team.

Your mission

  • You develop and implement customer-specific POS campaigns, activations and cooperations for drugstore shoppers
  • You own the roll-out of displays, secondary placements, POSM and furniture concepts in drugstores across Germany and Austria, including timings and in-store execution checks
  • You plan and manage retail media campaigns (onsite, offsite, in-store) in close alignment with our drugstore partners’ media networks
  • You enable KAM and field sales with clear briefings and manage design assets, content, agencies, display partners and other service providers
  • You measure activations and retail media against defined KPIs, optimize for impact and profitability, and feed best practices into our shopper marketing playbook
  • You work closely with Brand, KAM, field sales, Category Management and RGM and take on responsibility for part of the budget

Your experience & skills

  • You have a university degree, ideally in marketing, media or business
  • You have 2–3 years of experience in trade or shopper marketing, retail media or brand activation, ideally in the drugstore channel and/or with premium, beauty or luxury brands
  • You confidently manage projects, stakeholders and external partners
  • You work data-driven and are confident with KPIs, reporting tools and MS Office
  • You are hands-on, structured and have a keen eye for detail
  • You speak German and English fluently (business level) and are willing to travel occasionally, mainly to Hamburg, where most of the team is based

Why choose us?

Being part of our team means joining a high-performing company with a diverse and inclusive culture. In our fast-growing team of over 1,600 employees, we combine our passion for sports nutrition, supplements, and healthy foods with cutting-edge technology, production, and logistics processes. All of this serves one goal: providing our customers with top-quality products to support their healthy and active lifestyle.

You can look forward to a strong sense of team spirit, ongoing opportunities for professional growth and responsibility, and an exciting work environment that blends lifestyle and career. With locations in Germany (Hamburg, Elmshorn, Kaltenkirchen/Nützen, and Elsdorf) as well as international offices in London, Amsterdam, and Zug, Switzerland, TQG offers diverse career opportunities in areas such as technology, product development, sales, marketing, and logistics. Additionally, you’ll benefit from:

  • Flexible working hours and remote work options
  • Attractive employee discounts
  • Subsidy for the E-gym Wellpass
  • Workation
  • Corporate benefits
  • 28 days vacation/year
  • and much more

About Us

The Quality Group (TQG) is an innovative provider of sports nutrition products, bringing together the successful brands ESN and More Nutrition since 2021.

ESN has been the German market leader in sports nutrition since 2004, offering products like protein powders, bars, and supplements designed for ambitious fitness goals. Founded in 2017, More Nutrition focuses on healthy, reduced-sugar foods, providing solutions for conscious nutrition and weight management without compromise.

TQG’s vision is to help people become the best version of themselves. With passion and innovation, the company develops high-quality products that promote health, performance, and joy in life. Its agile company culture and exciting career opportunities make TQG a strong partner not only for customers but also for employees.

This is us – The Quality Group – nice to meet you! Now it’s your turn!
We look forward to your application! Regardless of gender, age, background, or identity – what matters to us is who you are and what you bring to the table. Join our team and grow with us!

¿Eres el Administrador de Base de Datos Oracle que Mantendrá el Corazón Tecnológico Interconectado y de Alto Rendimiento?

Creemos en el impacto real a través de la tecnología y nos posicionamos como socios estratégicos para la evolución digital de nuestros clientes.   • Dominio en administración de alta disponibilidad con Oracle RAC y Data Guard.

    • Cuentas con conocimientos en bases de datos NoSQL o de otros motores relacionales (PostgreSQL, MySQL).

jobs.description:
Job Title: Provider Credentialing Specialist
Primary Location: 100% Remote
Position Type: Contract (6 Months to 1 Year)

Overview
TalentFish is casting a line for a Provider Credentialing Specialist. This is a 6-month to 1-year full-time contract role, working 100% remote.

This position exists to support hands-on payer credentialing and provider enrollment, with a strong focus on behavioral health providers. The Credentialing Specialist will also play a key role in cleansing and validating credentialing data as the organization transitions to MD-Staff. We're looking for someone who has personally done the work, not just overseen or coordinated it. Contractors may be considered for permanent openings as opportunities arise.

What You Bring to the Role. (Ideal Experience)

  • 2+ years of direct, hands-on provider credentialing and/or payer enrollment experience.
  • Proven ability to independently manage payer enrollment end to end: preparing and submitting applications, tracking payer responses, resolving deficiencies, and maintaining provider participation records.
  • Experience credentialing and enrolling behavioral health providers (LCSWs, LPCs, psychologists, psychiatrists, etc.) and working within payer-specific requirements is strongly preferred.
  • Hands-on experience with Cactus and/or MD-Staff is strongly preferred; experience with both is ideal.
  • Experience with credentialing data cleansing, validation, reconciliation, and resolving duplicate or incomplete records, ideally as part of a system transition.
  • Working knowledge of initial credentialing, recredentialing, primary source verification, NPDB queries, CAQH profile maintenance and re-attestation, and Medicare/Medicaid revalidations.
  • Experience with CAQH and payer portals; strong computer and data-entry skills.
  • Strong attention to detail, organization, and the ability to manage a workload independently.
  • Clear, professional communication with providers, practices, payers, and internal teams, and a firm commitment to confidentiality.
  • High school diploma or GED required; associate degree preferred.
  • CPCS certification preferred.

What You'll Do. (Skills Used in this Position)

  • Process and track initial payer credentialing, provider enrollment, recredentialing, and revalidation applications for participating providers.
  • Support behavioral health provider credentialing and enrollment, including collecting and reviewing payer-required documentation.
  • Prepare, assemble, review, and quality-check provider applications, following up with providers and payers to resolve missing or inconsistent information.
  • Conduct credential verifications and mandated queries in line with organizational policy and payer requirements.
  • Enter, maintain, and update provider information in credentialing databases, CAQH, and payer systems.
  • Cleanse and validate credentialing and provider records to support the MD-Staff transition, flagging incomplete, outdated, or inconsistent data and coordinating corrections.
  • Monitor provider expirables, enrollment status, recredentialing deadlines, and payer revalidation cycles while keeping documentation and status tracking current.
  • Partner with providers, practice managers, medical staff offices, and payer representatives to keep credentialing and enrollment moving on time.
  • Prepare reports and updates for downstream billing and system maintenance, and help resolve enrollment-related claim issues.
  • Protect confidential provider information and follow privacy, compliance, and quality procedures.

Compensation Information
The expected salary range for this position is $25-28 per hour, depending on experience and qualifications. This role also qualifies for comprehensive benefits such as health insurance, 401(k), and paid time off. TalentFish is committed to pay transparency and equal opportunity. The salary range provided is in compliance with applicable state and federal regulations.
This role requires authorization to work in the U.S. without current or future visa sponsorship.
All offers are contingent upon the completion of a background check, which may include but is not limited to reference checks, education verification, employment verification, drug testing, criminal records checks, and any required certifications or compliance requirements based on the end client's background check policies and applicable laws.
TalentFish is an employee-owned company pioneering a new realm in talent acquisition. We are redefining IT staffing by evolving AI, video screening, and our unique platform. TalentFish focuses on providing the best employee, consultant, and client experience possible. At TalentFish we are an Equal Opportunity Employer; we embrace and encourage diversity!

This is Engineering at Lattice

Lattice’s Engineering team continuously works to better our product and our craft. We use a modern, cutting-edge tech stack and love experimenting with new technologies when they help us deliver great products to our customers. We strive for maintainable, robust, and performant code. We’re highly collaborative, continuously iterative, and work closely with designers and product managers. We prioritize not only great technical architecture but also an amazing product experience.

We’re looking for a product engineering leader who is passionate about delivering high-quality products and supporting the growth of our engineers. This is a unique opportunity to develop and scale key products across our product offering and contribute to the success of Lattice’s engineering organization.

What You Will Bring to the Table

You have 2+ years of experience directly managing software engineers. In this capacity, you have been responsible for defining roadmaps, shipping features and products, guiding and coaching the development of your direct reports and fostering a diverse, collaborative, and inclusive team culture.

  • You have a track record of planning engineering roadmaps and managing the day-to-day execution of engineering projects, culminating in releasing high quality features to customers.
  • You have experience collaborating with other engineering leaders and cross-functional team members.
  • You are comfortable with ambiguity, autonomy, and responsibility; you enjoy figuring out what needs to be done – and then doing it.
  • You have a proven ability to provide individual coaching, plan career development, and generally guide your team as they learn and grow.
  • You are kind and intellectually mature; equipped with the empathy, integrity, and technical ability required to earn the trust of an engineering team
  • You are an excellent written and verbal communicator who adapts effectively for executives, technical teams, and non-technical audiences.
  • Preferably, you have professional experience with the technologies with which we work (Node.js, React, Flow, GraphQL, Postgres, Amazon Web Services)

What You Will Do

  • You will lead your team in delivering AI-enabled products, taking new capabilities from prototype to production in a way that is reliable, trustworthy, and solves real customer problems.
  • You will develop a healthy and collaborative culture that embodies Lattice’s values.
  • You will help engineers grow and advance in their careers.
  • You will collaborate closely with the Lattice product team to define, plan, and prioritize our product roadmap. You will represent your team to the larger org. Ensure they receive public recognition for their success and take ownership of their failures.
  • You will set the direction for your team and plan for the long term, scaling our products upmarket while keeping the experience delightful and reliable for customers around the globe and maintaining a rapid pace of development.

___

Workforce & Systems Integration Manager

Georgia Center for Opportunity (GCO) is an independent, non-partisan policy research organization that develops solutions leading to social and economic opportunity in the state of Georgia and beyond. Our vision is to make vibrant communities where everyone can achieve their potential.

Our mission is to empower families to flourish across generations. We advance solutions that increase opportunity and create durable pathways to prosperity for Georgia’s families. To achieve our mission, we research ways to help remove barriers to opportunity in each of these pathways, promote our solutions to policymakers and the public, and help effective and innovative social enterprises deliver results in their communities. Our ultimate goal is to see every Georgian who is willing to seize the opportunities presented to them living a life that can be characterized as truly flourishing.

GCO is poised for growth, with an office in Peachtree Corners and programs in Gwinnett County and Columbus, Georgia, GCO is a fast-paced, entrepreneurial, and highly collaborative environment. The Workforce & Systems Integration Manager must be a self-starter, an independent worker, and a team player in this fast-growing organization.

This role reports to the Vice President of Program Strategy & Impact. The Workforce and Systems Integration Manager develops and manages the external partnerships, workforce strategies, and community resource networks that help participants and graduates achieve lasting family stability and economic mobility. Serving as the bridge between program delivery and the broader workforce ecosystem, this role ensures participants have coordinated access to education, financial literacy, employment opportunities, and other critical resources that support long-term flourishing.

This role identifies systemic barriers that limit graduate success and works collaboratively to reduce friction, improve alignment, and strengthen outcomes. Working throughout Georgia across both program areas, the manager identifies, cultivates and maintains relationships with workforce organizations, educational institutions, employers, public agencies, and/or community partners to create seamless pathways from learning to career advancement, employment, and sustained family well-being.

The Workforce and Systems Integration Manager also coordinates with the Program Insight & Impact Manager to utilize participant feedback to inform improvements to both programs and external systems by cultivating strategically targeted partnerships and leveraging graduate outcome data to support advancement, retention, wage growth, and continued opportunity throughout the partner network.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain relationships with workforce boards, educational institutions, vocational training providers, public agencies, and community organizations.
  • Build and steward workforce focused partnerships that create meaningful career pathways, advancement opportunities, and family-sustaining employment directly contributing to improved retention, wage growth, and family stability.
  • Collaborate with partners to understand workforce needs and translate those insights into program improvements.
  • Align external systems to reduce barriers and improve graduate access to opportunities across all program areas.
  • Communicate proactively to ensure graduates have coordinated access through these targeted partnerships to resources that promote economic mobility and family flourishing.
  • Support strategies that minimize the impact of benefits cliffs and other systemic barriers to advancement.
  • Collaborate with internal teams to ensure external partnerships strengthen program effectiveness and participant outcomes.
  • Represent the organization within workforce and community networks to advance the mission of economic mobility and family stability.
  • Coordinate with the Program Insight & Impact Manager to ensure participant outcomes consistently inform improvements to both program design and external partnerships.
  • Identify policy, system, and process barriers that affect participant success and inform the GCO policy team.

Qualifications

  • Demonstrates commitment to and alignment with GCO’s core values and strategic principles.
  • College degree or equivalent experience in a related field required
  • Record of integrity in managing sensitive and confidential information.
  • Minimum of 5 years of related work experience, including 2 or more years of proven community outreach and coordination experience.
  • Experience in Human Resources or Workforce Development preferred.
  • Demonstrates ability to build and maintain effective relationships with a wide range of stakeholders.
  • Strong relationship-building skills with employers, workforce partners, educational institutions, and community organizations.
  • Experience translating external opportunities into practical participant pathways.
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills (written and oral).
  • Ability to thrive in a fluid, unstructured, entrepreneurial environment.
  • Demonstrates systems thinking and the ability to connect people, organizations, and resources toward shared outcomes.
  • Comfort navigating ambiguity and influencing without direct authority.
  • Commitment to mission-driven decision making and continuous learning.
  • Ability to operationalize strategy into sustainable systems and partnerships.

Compensation & Benefits

GCO offers a competitive salary, commensurate with experience, and provides excellent benefits: health insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance, a 401k plan, life insurance, and paid time off. This position also offers the right candidate significant opportunities for professional development and growth.

We are looking for people who share our values of innovation, passion, excellence, and impact. For more on GCO, go to www.foropportunity.org.

jobs.title: Ingénieure ou Ingénieur, Sécurité physique
jobs.excerpt: Vous vous joindrez à une équipe spécialisée qui conçoit des systèmes de sécurité électronique intégrés pour des projets complexes au Canada et aux États-Unis.
jobs.description:
Vous vous joindrez à une équipe spécialisée qui conçoit des systèmes de sécurité électronique intégrés pour des projets complexes au Canada et aux États-Unis. Le poste s’adresse à une ingénieure ou à un ingénieur comptant de 4 à 10 années d’expérience, capable de prendre en charge des volets techniques définis, de la définition des besoins jusqu’au soutien à la construction et à la mise en service.

Vous pourrez travailler à partir du bureau Stantec de votre choix, en télétravail à temps plein ou en combinant librement les journées au bureau et en télétravail, selon les modalités applicables au poste.

Des projets qui comptent

Vous travaillerez sur des projets où votre expertise servira à protéger les personnes, les biens et les infrastructures, notamment dans les secteurs suivants :

  • les installations gouvernementales fédérales, provinciales et municipales, la défense, les ambassades et les postes frontaliers;

  • la justice et la sécurité publique : palais de justice, établissements de détention et installations policières;

  • les infrastructures de transport, d’énergie (électricité et gaz naturel), d’eau et autres services essentiels, y compris les installations maritimes comme les ports et les écluses;

  • les centres de données, centres de contrôle, installations de radiotélédiffusion et environnements technologiques critiques;

  • les établissements de santé et d’enseignement ainsi que les installations de recherche et développement;

  • les installations industrielles, minières, aéronautiques et commerciales.

Votre rôle

Sous la direction d’un ingénieur principal ou du responsable de discipline, vous prendrez en charge des volets techniques définis et agirez comme interlocuteur technique auprès du client et des autres disciplines du projet. Selon votre niveau d’expérience et votre degré d’autonomie, vous pourrez aussi prendre en charge des mandats de plus petite envergure. Vous transformerez les objectifs de sécurité, les contraintes d’exploitation et les résultats d’évaluations des risques en solutions d’ingénierie cohérentes, réalisables et documentées.

Orientations techniques et conseils au client

  • Analyser les besoins fonctionnels et techniques à partir des exigences du client, des recommandations issues d’évaluations des risques et des menaces, des études de sécurité et des programmes fonctionnels et techniques.

  • Définir, avec l’ingénieur principal, les concepts de sécurité, les critères de performance, les stratégies d’intégration et les limites de portée entre les disciplines.

  • Préparer les options, les risques, les coûts et les compromis techniques à présenter aux décideurs, et formuler des recommandations claires.

Conception de systèmes de sécurité intégrés

  • Concevoir, planifier et documenter des solutions de contrôle d’accès, de détection d’intrusion, de vidéosurveillance, d’intercommunication, de gestion des clés, de gestion des visiteurs et d’autres applications spécialisées.

  • Développer les interfaces entre les sous-systèmes de sécurité, les systèmes de bâtiment, les réseaux de télécommunications et les outils d’exploitation.

  • Intégrer, lorsque requis, les contrôles de véhicules et de piétons, les solutions biométriques et les technologies émergentes en fonction du besoin réel et du contexte d’utilisation.

  • Effectuer des relevés de sites existants, valider les contraintes et établir des concepts adaptés aux opérations, aux infrastructures et aux étapes de réalisation.

Espaces opérationnels et infrastructures associées

  • Concevoir, en collaboration avec les autres disciplines, les centres de contrôle des opérations, postes de garde, salles d’équipements et postes de travail en tenant compte de l’ergonomie, des flux opérationnels, de la continuité des opérations et de la maintenabilité.

  • Coordonner les besoins en câblage, télécommunications, alimentation normale et de secours, locaux techniques, interfaces de portes et résilience des systèmes, avec l’appui de nos équipes internes spécialisées en infrastructures de télécommunications, électricité, structure, mécanique et architecture.

Documents d’ingénierie et assurance qualité

  • Préparer et réviser les rapports de conception, schémas de zonage, diagrammes fonctionnels, schémas-blocs, plans, devis, cahiers des charges, estimations budgétaires et documents d’appel d’offres.

  • Coordonner le travail de production avec les collègues et les techniciens, et veiller à la qualité, à la cohérence et à la traçabilité des livrables.

  • Produire les documents d’ingénierie et, lorsque requis, les signer et les sceller pour les volets dont vous avez la responsabilité, conformément aux règles de l’Ordre des ingénieurs du Québec et aux exigences applicables au projet.

  • Appliquer les codes, normes, exigences réglementaires et critères propres à la clientèle.

Appels d’offres, construction et mise en service

  • Soutenir les clients durant les appels d’offres, analyser les soumissions et les écarts techniques, et formuler des recommandations.

  • Répondre aux demandes d’information, examiner les dessins d’atelier et soutenir l’équipe de surveillance pendant la construction.

  • Réaliser des inspections et des essais fonctionnels, participer aux activités de mise en service et assurer le suivi de la résolution des déficiences, selon la portée du mandat.

  • Maintenir des relations de travail efficaces avec les clients, les équipes de projet, les entrepreneurs et les fournisseurs

jobs.description:
Team Associate I

Office of Student Affairs

Non Exempt, Contingent II, Full Time, Pay Grade 007

Job location: Remote

JOB SUMMARY

Under direct supervision, performs the full range of multi-functional clerical/operational duties as part of an institutionally defined self-directed team. Work involves a broad variety of specialized tasks and methods consistent with a clearly defined team-based work environment and continuous quality improvement objectives. Participates in providing guidance and instruction to Team Assistants.


PRIMARY DUTIES

  • Receives and directs incoming calls and visitors. Responds to general inquiries requiring research or interpretation of relevant departmental policies and procedures. Makes referrals to other team members or teams as appropriate.
  • Maintains manual and automated record-keeping and filing systems. Codes, sorts, processes, and files the full range of team documents and materials. Assembles, enters, edits, and retrieves data and records.
  • Operates office equipment such as multi-line telephones, personal computers, typewriters, facsimile machines, and photocopiers.
  • Prepares worksheets, tables, correspondence, and standard reports. Participates in the preparation and review of statistical and other reports for completeness and accuracy.
  • Identifies and resolves clerical process problems impacting productivity and quality. Participates in developing new or revised processes.
  • Assists in planning and coordinating team clerical work. Coordinates work flow of assigned clerical tasks or function.

Note: The intent of this list of primary duties is to provide a representative summary of the major duties and responsibilities of this job. Incumbents perform other related duties assigned. Specific duties and responsibilities may vary based upon departmental needs.

ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Conduct calls to students using the Five 9 telephony system and dialer and follow standard operating procedures for each call.
  • Respond to student and staff emails collaboratively and with excellent internal and external customer service.
  • Provide excellent customer service in speaking with students and identifying any challenges that the student had that prevented them from finishing their program.
  • Encourage and motivate students to overcome challenges to finish their program and reach their goals.
  • Coordinate the warm transfer and hand off, of students to a Success Coach, Financial Solutions Advisor, or other department to work with the student to resolve issues or enroll into a course.
  • Verify and capture student information and document completely in the CRM. Submit cases for any needed resolution or issue.
  • Provide support and resolution to enrollment inquiries made by phone or through email, cases, in person, chat and other established means of communication.
  • Other duties as assigned to support University wide initiatives such as training, attending meetings and presenting ideas to colleagues or guests will also be required.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Education: High School Diploma or GED.

Experience: Three years in clerical work.


REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE/SKILLS/ABILITIES

  • General knowledge of team office practices, procedures, and equipment; of grammar, spelling, and punctuation.
  • Skill in independently performing a broad range of team clerical and operational tasks including computer data entry, basic arithmetic calculations and compilation of statistical data; completion of standard forms, creation and maintenance of paper and computer files, preparation of standard reports and data summaries, and responding to requests for general information.
  • Skill in effective telephone usage.
  • Ability to work effectively in a self-directed team-based work environment; to understand and apply team quality and performance standards.
  • Ability to plan and independently perform specialized clerical tasks; operate all team office equipment; to communicate both orally and in writing; to follow oral and written procedures and processes; to establish and maintain effective work relationships both within and outside the team; to operate personal computers and software; to understand and interpret department policies and procedures; to provide guidance and instruction to Team Assistants.

All submissions should include a cover letter and resume.

The University of Maryland Global Campus (UMGC) is an equal opportunity employer and complies with all applicable federal and state laws regarding nondiscrimination. UMGC is committed to a policy of equal opportunity for all persons and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, age, marital status, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, disability, religion, ancestry, political affiliation or veteran status in employment, educational programs and activities, and admissions.

Workplace Accommodations:

The University of Maryland Global Campus Global Campus (UMGC) is committed to creating and maintaining a welcoming and inclusive working environment for people of all abilities. UMGC is dedicated to the principle that no qualified individual with a disability shall, based on disability, be excluded from participation in or be denied the benefits of the services, programs, or activities of the University, or be subjected to discrimination. For information about UMGC’s Reasonable Workplace Accommodation Policy or to request an accommodation, applicants/candidates can contact Employee Accommodations via email .

Benefits Package Highlights:

  • Generous Time Off: Enjoy 14 days of paid vacation, 15 days of sick leave, 3 personal days, and 16 paid holidays (17 during general election years).Time off rates will be prorated based on the number of hours worked.

  • Comprehensive Health Coverage: Access to health care, medical with vision, dental, and prescription plans for both individuals and families, effective from the 1st of the month following your hire date. Contingent II employees who work on average 30 or more hours per week (130 hours per month) are eligible for subsidized state of Maryland medical and prescription benefits. Contingent II employees who work on average less than 30 hours per week but at least 20 hours per week are eligible for a stipend to assist in the purchase of a health plan.

  • Insurance Options: Term Life Insurance, Accidental Death and Dismemberment Insurance, and Long-Term Disability (LTD) Insurance. NOTE: CII Part-time employees working less than 0.5 FTE are not eligible for LTD.

  • Retirement Stipend: Contingent II employees receive a retirement stipend equal to 7.25 percent of their base salary and are eligible to contribute to a supplemental retirement account (SRA).

  • Supplemental Retirement Plans: include 401(k), 403(b), 457(b), and various Roth options. The university does not provide subsidies or matching funds.

  • Tuition Remission: CII employees are eligible immediately for Tuition Remission at UMGC or at University of Maryland College Park. Spouses and dependent children are eligible for undergraduate tuition remission after two years of service. NOTE: For part-time employees (at least 50 percent of the time), tuition remission benefits are prorated.

jobs.title: Industry Strategy Lead, PLM
jobs.excerpt: About CoLabAt CoLab, we help mechanical engineering teams bring life-changing products to market years sooner.
jobs.description:
About CoLab

At CoLab, we help mechanical engineering teams bring life-changing products to market years sooner.

CoLab is the AI platform for driving stronger engineering decisions. Every design review in CoLab builds a knowledge repository of design feedback, decisions, and lessons learned - which AI agents draw from to flag issues on future designs before they compound. The more your team works in CoLab, the smarter it gets and the faster you arrive at the ideal design. Companies like Ford, Komatsu, and Johnson Controls use CoLab to catch issues earlier, eliminate rework cycles, and bring products to market faster.

Founded in St. John’s, Newfoundland, CoLab has grown quickly from our first customer in 2019 to a rapidly scaling company. We’ve recently been recognized on Deloitte’s Fast 50™ and Fast 500™, and named a Canadian company to watch by The Globe and Mail and Financial Post.

Role Summary

This role is a high-leverage operator reporting into the Director of Industry Strategy & Transformation, with direct exposure to revenue leadership and account owners. This role exists to define how CoLab wins and grows inside the PLM ecosystems our customers already run, turning Windchill, Teamcenter, and 3DEXPERIENCE environments into a path to enterprise adoption rather than a reason to stall.

Every enterprise engineering organization we work with has a PLM strategy, a team that owns it, and a long list of programs competing for its attention. Design decisions get made in reviews and typically land in PLM, and the gap between the two is where context gets lost, changes get re-litigated, and engineering teams lose hours every week. You will define how CoLab works with PLM, earn the trust of the IT and digital engineering leaders who own those systems, and turn PLM alignment into a repeatable advantage across the revenue org.

This is a deal-facing, customer-facing, and product-influencing role. The right person is part strategist, part operator, part competitor. Someone who can read a room of executives, build a hyper compelling value case on the fly, speak credibly to the PLM owner and the VP of Engineering in the same meeting, and close out the next step before the meeting ends.

Responsibilities

  • Define and own CoLab’s PLM strategy, including how we position alongside Windchill, Teamcenter, 3DEXPERIENCE, and the rest of the engineering stack, and how design review decisions flow into the digital thread our customers are building.
  • Map the PLM landscape inside strategic accounts, identifying who owns the roadmap, where modernization or migration programs are underway, and where review, change, and release processes break down between engineering and the system of record.
  • Build the value case for PLM and IT leaders, why CoLab strengthens their PLM investment rather than competing with it, grounded in change cycle time, ECO quality, data continuity, and adoption across engineering.
  • Run executive, IT, and engineering workshops that expose workflow friction between design reviews and PLM processes and create the urgency needed to mobilize multi-stakeholder buying groups.
  • Collaborate on deal strategy for strategic opportunities where PLM and IT sit in the buying group, partnering with account executives to coach champions, navigate architecture and security reviews, and build the executive narratives that move buying groups forward.
  • Shape CoLab’s relationships with PLM vendors and systems integrators, identifying where partnerships open doors, where they create a co-sell motion, and where they need to be managed carefully.
  • Package PLM plays that account executives and customer engineers can run without you in the room, from discovery angles by platform to integration-led expansion sequences.
  • Synthesize signals from strategic accounts into structured product feedback on integrations and the connected PLM experience, and validate product concepts with key customers so new capabilities fit how PLM-driven organizations actually work.
  • Support the Director of Industry Strategy & Transformation with boots on the ground market trends, competitive dynamics, and customer insights across the PLM ecosystem.

Who You Are

  • A mechanical engineer by background, with real-world experience in product development, engineering processes, and design collaboration.
  • You’ve lived PLM from the inside. You have a deep understanding of the industry. You bring direct experience owning PLM strategy, implementation, or operations at a manufacturer, a PLM vendor, or a systems integrator, with hands-on depth in at least one of Windchill, Teamcenter, or 3DEXPERIENCE. You know how change management, BOM, and release processes actually run, and you can talk architecture with IT and workflow with engineering.
  • You see the whole stack. You understand where PLM, CAD, ERP, MES, and point tools meet, where the digital thread breaks in practice, and how to position a new platform so it strengthens what a customer already owns.
  • High emotional intelligence and the ability to read a room of executives in real time. You know when to push, when to pause, when to ask the harder question, and when to take the win and move on.
  • Competitive by nature. You are wired to play to win, you put in the reps, and you run at high cadence. You take losses personally enough to learn from them but not personally enough to slow down.
  • Strong context switching ability. You can move from a board level value conversation to a PLM architecture review to a workflow mapping session back to back and bring the right focus to each one.
  • Sharp sense of time value. You understand which work compounds, which work is throwaway, and which conversations are worth a calendar hold versus a quick Slack. You make calls and you move.
  • Strong commercial acumen and the ability to translate technical capability into business outcomes that resonate with VPs of Engineering, CIOs and PLM leaders, CEOs, and CFOs.
  • Operationally wired. You understand how work actually gets done inside complex organizations. You can spot process drag, identify where reviews break down, and connect workflow-level friction to business-level cost. You don’t just diagnose, you translate it into a path forward.
  • Clear, direct communicator. You write concisely, present without filler, and can build a clean, compelling deck under pressure. You know that a strong deck is a forcing function, not a deliverable, and you build them that way.
  • Fluent with AI tools as a force multiplier. You know how to use AI to compress research, sharpen messaging, and build faster. You don’t just tolerate the tools, you intentionally reach for them to do more with less.

What Success Looks Like in Year One

  • You have defined CoLab’s PLM strategy, and PLM and IT leaders at multiple strategic accounts are actively supporting CoLab as a result.
  • You are owning PLM and transformation workshops with our top enterprise accounts.
  • Your PLM plays are in use across the revenue team, with partner-sourced or integration-led pipeline you can point to.
  • You have meaningfully influenced and supported the outcome of multiple seven figure deals.
  • You are trusted to drive customer conversations without backup.

jobs.description:
What You’ll Do

Role Summary

The Support Tax Technologist serves as the strategic bridge between Avalara’s product vision and the real-world needs of enterprise customers. This role combines deep tax technology expertise, enterprise ERP integration knowledge, and advanced troubleshooting capabilities to help customers maximize the value of Avalara solutions.

The Support Tax Technologist works closely with large enterprise customers to understand complex business requirements, uncover real-world use cases, and translate tax and compliance requirements into scalable, integrated solutions. Acting as both a technical advisor and domain expert, this role provides expert guidance on Avalara’s platform, enterprise integrations, and compliance automation capabilities while bringing field insights back to Product, Engineering teams to influence solution development and improve customer outcomes.

The role also plays a critical part in post-implementation customer success by partnering closely with the Implementation Tax Technologist team during hypercare and customer handoff, ensuring continuity, adoption, and long-term operational success.

How This Role Elevates Avalara

From a business perspective, the Support Tax Technologist strengthens Avalara’s relationships with large enterprise customers by helping them design, deploy, and optimize scalable compliance solutions embedded within their operational systems. Through deep technical and tax expertise, this role improves customer retention, supports expansion opportunities, and increases confidence in Avalara’s ability to solve complex compliance challenges.

For our teams, the Support Tax Technologist serves as a key conduit between customers, partners, Product, Engineering, and Support teams. By surfacing customer insights, identifying recurring integration and configuration challenges, and providing structured feedback, this role helps shape product enhancements, improve support readiness, and reduce operational friction. The role also drives internal enablement through coaching, office hours, knowledge sharing, and training programs that elevate the capabilities of customer-facing teams.

For customers, the Support Tax Technologist acts as a trusted advisor who combines tax domain expertise with technical integration knowledge. By helping customers automate, scale, and de-risk compliance processes, this role enables organizations to move beyond periodic tax filing activities toward continuous, embedded compliance across their ERP, eCommerce, billing, and financial systems.

What Your Responsibilities Will Be

Responsibilities

  • Engage directly with enterprise customers and partners through the support case process to assist with integration challenges and compliance automation objectives.
  • Provide subject matter expertise for Avalara solutions and integrations.
  • Translate tax requirements, including sales and use tax, VAT, exemptions, returns, e-invoicing, and other compliance obligations into configurable and scalable technology solutions.
  • Deliver expert support for Avalara enterprise ERP integrations and associated business workflows.
  • Handle escalated customer issues and critical support situations, leading root cause analysis, coordinating internal stakeholders, and ensuring timely resolution.
  • Collaborate with customers to understand technical challenges, identify root causes, and implement comprehensive long-term solutions.
  • Design and recommend scalable compliance architectures that enable customers to embed compliance into their operational systems rather than relying on manual tax processes.
  • Partner closely with Product and Engineering teams by delivering structured customer feedback and insights that influence product direction and solution development.
  • Support post-implementation hypercare activities and work closely with the Implementation Tax Technologist team to ensure seamless handoff and long-term customer success.
  • Lead customer-facing training programs, webinars, and enablement sessions for enterprise customers and strategic partners.
  • Drive internal enablement by evaluating recurring customer questions and conducting weekly office hours sessions for Global Support Organization (GSO) teams.
  • Develop and maintain best practices, technical documentation, integration guidance, and knowledge resources that improve organizational effectiveness.

12-month Success Signals

  • Demonstrable expertise in at least one enterprise ERP platform and serves as a recognized internal subject matter expert.
  • Reduces recurring support issues by identifying systemic integration, configuration, and process challenges and driving long-term solutions.
  • Successfully supports seamless post-implementation transitions and hypercare engagements for enterprise customers, resulting in improved adoption and customer satisfaction.
  • Delivers measurable improvements in customer adoption, platform utilization, and operational compliance outcomes.
  • Influences multiple product enhancements or process improvements through structured feedback gathered from customer and partner interactions.
  • Successfully conducts customer webinars, training sessions, and enablement programs that increase customer knowledge and self-service capabilities.
  • Establishes highly utilized internal office hours and coaching programs that improve support readiness and technical proficiency in ERP integration best practices.
  • Contributes to scalable compliance strategies that help customers move from traditional tax filing activities to embedded, automated compliance operations.

What You'll Need to be Successful

AI Expectations

Avalara is an AI-first company.

We expect every employee, manager, and leader to actively leverage AI to enhance productivity, quality, innovation, and customer value. AI is embedded in our workflows, decision-making, and products — and success at Avalara requires embracing AI as an essential capability, not an optional tool.

AI Bar Raiser Expectations

A successful Support Tax Technologist will:

  • Continuously evaluate emerging AI capabilities within enterprise ERP systems, and recommend innovative applications that improve customer outcomes and organizational effectiveness.
  • Demonstrate advanced, applied AI expertise to improve customer diagnostics, technical analysis, integration troubleshooting, and compliance solution recommendations.
  • Leverage AI to accelerate root cause analysis, customer issue resolution, and knowledge creation while maintaining accuracy and compliance standards.
  • Identify opportunities to use AI to improve customer enablement, training delivery, technical documentation, and operational efficiency.
  • Quantify AI-driven outcomes through measurable improvements in resolution speed, knowledge reuse, automation, customer satisfaction, and support effectiveness.
  • Share AI best practices and coach peers on effective AI adoption within technical support and customer-facing workflows.
  • Drive responsible AI usage while ensuring customer data security, compliance, and governance requirements are maintained.

We are looking for a Support Tax Technologist to raise the bar for Avalara and our customers through:

  • Elevating team capability and customer outcomes through technical leadership, knowledge sharing, coaching, and practical guidance on enterprise integrations, compliance automation, and support best practices.
  • Demonstrating strong ownership and accountability for complex, high-impact customer issues, especially in escalated and cross-functional situations, and modeling calm, thorough, end-to-end resolution leadership.
  • Improving systems, processes, and documentation so enterprise support motions become more scalable, consistent, and effective over time.
  • Simplifying complex tax, compliance, and technical integration challenges into actionable guidance that improves internal execution and helps customers operate with greater confidence.
  • Challenging assumptions constructively and identifying better approaches that reduce friction, strengthen support readiness, and improve long-term customer success.
  • Leaving every customer engagement, internal partnership, and operational process stronger than they found it by contributing insights, enablement, and durable improvements that increase organizational effectiveness.

Qualifications

  • Education
    • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field.
  • Experience
    • Minimum of 5 years of experience in tax technology implementation, enterprise application support, ERP integrations, technical consulting, or technical support within the compliance automation industry.
    • Experience supporting large enterprise customers and complex technical environments.
    • Experience working with enterprise ERP systems, with subject matter expertise in at least one major ERP platform.
    • Experience supporting cloud-based business applications and SaaS platforms.
    • Experience with tax and compliance technology solutions, including sales and use tax, VAT, exemptions, returns, and related compliance processes.
    • Experience in accounting, tax operations, tax technology, or related compliance services.
    • Experience assessing and mitigating risks related to sales and local tax (SALT) compliance.
    • Experience supporting customer escalations, leading cross-functional problem resolution efforts, and managing complex technical issues.
  • Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
    • Deep understanding of Avalara solutions, compliance automation principles, and enterprise integration architectures.
    • Very strong knowledge of enterprise ERP systems, business process workflows, and integration best practices.
    • Working knowledge of networking concepts, APIs, middleware technologies, and cloud-based application ecosystems.
    • Ability to quickly learn, configure, and support cloud-based business platforms and financial system interactions.
    • Ability to translate complex tax requirements into scalable, automated technology solutions.
    • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and root cause analysis skills.
    • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate effectively with technical, operational, tax, and executive stakeholders.
    • Ability to influence cross-functional teams and drive alignment across multiple organizations.
    • Strong customer relationship management and consultative problem-solving capabilities.
    • Ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining a high standard of customer service and technical excellence.

Avalara is an AI-first Company

AI is embedded in our workflows, decision-making, and products. Success here requires embracing AI as an essential capability.

  • You’ll bring experience using AI and AI-related technologies, ready to thrive here.

  • You’ll apply AI every day to business challenges - improving efficiency, contributing solutions, and driving results for your team, our company, and our customers.

  • You’ll grow with AI by staying curious about new trends and best practices, and by sharing what you learn so others can benefit too.

How We'll Take Care of You

Total Rewards

In addition to a great compensation package, paid time off, and paid parental leave, many Avalara employees are eligible for bonuses.

Health & Wellness Benefits vary by location but generally include private medical, life, and disability insurance.

Inclusive culture and diversity Avalara strongly supports diversity, equity, and inclusion, and is committed to integrating them into our business practices and our organizational culture. We also have a total of 8 employee-run resource groups, each with senior leadership and exec sponsorship.

What You Need To Know About Avalara

We’re defining the relationship between tax and tech.

We’ve already built an industry-leading cloud compliance platform, processing over 54 billion customer API calls and over 6.6 million tax returns a year. Our growth is real - we're a billion dollar business - and we’re not slowing down until we’ve achieved our mission - to be part of every transaction in the world.

We’re bright, innovative, and disruptive, like the orange we love to wear. It captures our quirky spirit and optimistic mindset. It shows off the culture we’ve designed, that empowers our people to win. We’ve been different from day one. Join us, and your career will be too.

We’re An Equal Opportunity Employer

Supporting diversity and inclusion is a cornerstone of our company — we don’t want people to fit into our culture, but to enrich it. All qualified candidates will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, age, gender, national orientation, disability, sexual orientation, US Veteran status, or any other factor protected by law. jobs.excerpt: About TreeringAt Treering, we help people capture and preserve life’s most meaningful moments — from school milestones to unforgettable travel experiences.
jobs.description:
About Treering

At Treering, we help people capture and preserve life’s most meaningful moments — from school milestones to unforgettable travel experiences. Our innovative memory-as-a-service platform combines intuitive, AI-enabled tools with a seamless user experience to make creating personalized keepsakes easy and joyful. We’re a fast-growing, purpose-driven company expanding beyond yearbooks into travel and experiential memories, and we’re equally intentional about creating a workplace where people feel supported, empowered, and connected to the impact of their work.

About the role

    You'll be Treering's first dedicated UX researcher. There's no research team, playbook, or backlog of studies waiting for you. You'll build the practice from the ground up and make the voice of our customers part of how we decide what to build.


    You'll report to the Head of User Experience and split your time between our core yearbook business and new products built for the schools and families we already serve. This is a remote role based in the US.

What you'll do

  • Understand our four core audiences. Lead foundational research with yearbook editors, parents, students, and photography partners to understand their behaviors, goals, frustrations, and unmet needs.

  • Test ideas before we build them. Conduct generative research to find new opportunities and evaluative research to validate concepts, prototypes, and new product bets early, so we invest in what people will actually use and pay for.

  • Build an ongoing listening practice. Establish a steady rhythm of customer interviews and surveys, and analyze existing data, like product feedback and support tickets, to identify opportunities for improvement.

  • Empower the team. Build an insights repository the whole company can use, so findings reach further and keep informing the product.

  • Partner with analytics. Work hand in hand with our product analytics effort, pairing what people do with why they do it.

  • Tell the story. Share actionable findings and recommendations in ways that move product designers, product managers, engineers, and executives to act.

  • Set the foundation. Establish research standards, tools, and processes, including how we recruit participants and how we research responsibly with schools and families.

Who you'll work with

    You'll work closely with product designers, product managers, engineers, our customer success team, and the analytics effort. Our teams are small, so your insights will reach the people building the product directly.

What success looks like

    In your first 90 days: You're talking with customers on a regular rhythm. Foundational studies are underway with yearbook editors and parents. An insights repository is up and running.

    In your first year: Research is a regular part of how Treering makes product decisions, and the team has an easy, ongoing way to hear from the people we serve.

What you bring

  • 5+ years of UX research experience, with qualitative methods as your core strength. You're an exceptional interviewer and listener.

  • Comfort conducting surveys and working with behavioral data, analytics tools and A/B test results, though the ability to do advanced quantitative analyses is not required.

  • Experience using AI tools to speed up research and improve its quality.

  • A track record of planning and running qualitative studies that shaped product or business decisions.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including strong storytelling, with the ability to influence stakeholders at all levels.

  • Experience working with a cross-functional team including product managers, designers, and developers.

Bonus points

  • A background in EdTech or K-12, including working within school privacy and access constraints.

  • Research with children, including age-appropriate methods and consent/assent practices.

  • Work on consumer or e-commerce products, especially purchase flows.

  • Familiarity with B2B2C products, where you sell to organizations and serve the people inside and around them.

  • Time as a first or solo researcher, building a practice without an existing playbook.

  • Hands-on experience setting up research operations, such as participant recruiting and insights repositories.

Location, travel, and compensation

  • Location: Remote, US-based

  • Travel: Occasional travel to schools and to meet with the team

Senior FDA Compliance Analyst

Reports to: Head of Third Party Services

Position Summary

The Senior FDA Compliance Analyst supports FDA regulatory compliance across the organization's multi-site fertility network. Reporting to the Head of Third Party Services, this position serves as a subject matter resource for FDA requirements related to third party reproduction and supports the development, implementation, and monitoring of consistent regulatory processes.

The Analyst plays a key role in transitioning the organization toward a centralized FDA compliance model, with a focus on regulatory oversight, policy development, staff education, auditing, inspection readiness, and new practice integration.

Core Responsibilities

FDA Regulatory Compliance

  • Serve as a subject matter resource for FDA requirements applicable to third party reproduction.
  • Monitor regulatory changes, assess operational impacts, and communicate updates to appropriate stakeholders.
  • Provide guidance on donor eligibility, screening, testing, documentation, quarantine, release, and recordkeeping.
  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders and external regulatory partners to address compliance questions and concerns.

Program Development & Standardization

  • Support the development and implementation of a centralized FDA compliance model across the network.
  • Assess existing workflows, identify regulatory and operational gaps, and recommend process improvements.
  • Develop and maintain standardized policies, consents, SOPs, work instructions, and documentation requirements.
  • Support consistent application of FDA requirements while accounting for appropriate practice-level differences.
  • Identify opportunities to optimize technology, workflows, and centralized support processes.

Auditing & Compliance Monitoring

  • Support the development and execution of an internal FDA audit program.
  • Conduct routine and targeted audits to identify compliance gaps, documentation deficiencies, and operational risks.
  • Prepare audit findings and recommendations and assist with corrective and preventive action plans.
  • Track corrective actions through resolution and monitor recurring issues.
  • Maintain compliance metrics and provide regular updates to the Head of Third Party Services.

FDA Inspection Readiness

  • Support ongoing FDA inspection readiness across applicable practices.
  • Conduct readiness assessments, mock inspections, and documentation reviews.
  • Serve as a key resource during FDA inspections, coordinating documentation, communication, and follow-up activities.
  • Assist with responses to regulatory observations and corrective actions.
  • Maintain inspection records and share lessons learned across the network.

Education & Training

  • Develop and deliver standardized FDA compliance education and training.
  • Support onboarding, ongoing education, and competency development for staff involved in FDA-regulated activities.
  • Provide targeted education in response to regulatory changes, audit findings, and identified knowledge gaps.
  • Serve as an ongoing resource for staff questions related to FDA requirements.

Integration & New Practice Support

  • Participate in FDA compliance assessments during acquisition due diligence and support transition planning for newly integrated practices.
  • Support FDA compliance assessments for new practice acquisitions and integrations.
  • Review current-state workflows, policies, documentation, and systems to identify gaps.
  • Assist with transition plans to align new practices with the organization's centralized FDA compliance model.
  • Coordinate implementation of required workflows, SOPs, tools, and training.
  • Provide go-live and post-implementation support and monitor adoption.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in regulatory affairs, life sciences, healthcare administration, quality management, business administration, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.
  • Experience in FDA-regulated reproductive medicine, tissue banking, third party reproduction, or a comparable regulatory environment.
  • Knowledge of FDA requirements related to reproductive tissue and donor eligibility.
  • Experience developing and maintaining regulatory policies, SOPs, and workflows.
  • Experience conducting compliance audits, supporting regulatory inspections, and tracking corrective actions.
  • Ability to interpret regulatory requirements and translate them into practical operational processes.
  • Ability to independently prioritize work, manage multiple projects simultaneously, and exercise sound judgment when evaluating regulatory and operational risks.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, communication, and project management skills.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively across multiple practices and departments.

Preferred

  • Experience with donor egg, donor sperm, embryo donation, gestational carrier, or other third party reproductive services.
  • Experience supporting FDA compliance across a multi-site healthcare organization.
  • Experience with centralized compliance programs, practice integrations, and regulatory process improvement.
  • Experience developing compliance education and supporting FDA inspections.

Your work will help establish reusable platform capabilities, implementation patterns, evaluation practices, and operational standards for agentic applications. By improving the reliability, accuracy, security, and scalability of these systems, you will enable faster delivery of Aviator and other agentic efforts while reducing duplicated engineering effort across teams.   • Aviator and other priority agentic initiatives are using production-grade platform capabilities owned or significantly shaped by this role.
  • Reusable frameworks, libraries, or service patterns reduce the time required for Avalara teams to build and launch agentic workflows.

The successful candidate will hold themselves and others to high standards, simplify complexity, challenge assumptions respectfully, use data in decision-making, and leave systems, processes, and teams stronger than they found them.

jobs.title: Clinical Documentation Quality Reviewer
jobs.excerpt: At Memorial Hermann, we pursue a common goal of delivering high quality, efficient care while creating exceptional experiences for every member of our community.
jobs.description:
At Memorial Hermann, we pursue a common goal of delivering high quality, efficient care while creating exceptional experiences for every member of our community. When we say every member of our community, that includes our employees. We know that when our employees feel cared for, heard and valued, they are inspired to create moments that exceed expectations, while prioritizing safety, compassion, personalization and efficiency. If you want to advance your career and contribute to our vision of creating healthier communities, now and for generations to come, we want you to be a part of our team.

Job Summary

The Clinical Documentation Integrity (CDI) Quality Reviewer responsibilities include comprehensive secondary clinical chart reviews to identify potential missed opportunities for documentation clarification, act as a liaison between coding and CDI to resolve Diagnosis-Related Group (DRG) or other code discrepancies, collaborate with CDI educator to educate CDI team based on opportunities identified in second level reviews and work directly with clinicians and providers to improve the overall quality and completeness of documentation through the query process and/or provider education. The CDI Quality Reviewer will collaborate closely with Coders, Coding Quality Auditors, Quality Department and Providers to assure documentation is clinically appropriate, accurately reflects the severity of illness and risk of mortality for the patient and is reflective of current CMS or other regulatory standards. Typically reports to the CDI Quality/Education Manager.

Job Description

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Education: Bachelor's of Nursing, required; Master’s Degree in Nursing or Management preferred.

Licenses/Certifications:

  • Current State of Texas license or temporary/compact license to practice professional nursing
  • One of the following is required:
    • Certified Clinical Documentation Specialist (CCDS) from the Association of Clinical Documentation Improvement Specialists
    • Certified Clinical Documentation Integrity Professional (CDIP) from the American Health Information Management Association (AHIMA)
    • Certified Coding Specialist (CCS) from the American Health Information Management Association (AHIMA)

Experience / Knowledge / Skills:

  • Three (3) years of Clinical Documentation Integrity (CDI) experience required
  • Approved AHIMA ICD-10-CM/PCS Trainer preferred
  • Previous CDIS auditing, denial and Vizient experience preferred
  • Strong computer proficiency including working knowledge of MS Office- Word, Excel and Outlook and 3M Coding and Reimbursement software; experience with Epic EMR preferred
  • Excellent communication, analytical and problem-solving skills are essential
  • Strong organizational skills and must be detail oriented
  • Highly analytical with strong risk assessment, impact analysis and problem- solving skills
  • Highly self-motivated, yet demonstrate ability to be a team player and take direction
  • Flexible and able to multi-task and prioritize daily workload, performing concurrent chart reviews as needed

PRINCIPAL ACCOUNTABILITIES

  • Completes comprehensive, clinical secondary reviews of targeted patient populations to include cases with DRG and/or code discrepancies; mortality reviews to ensure documentation supports risk of mortality; hospital acquired conditions (HACs), patient safety indicators (PSIs) or other top priority diagnoses as identified for potential missed opportunities to clarify documentation or clinically validate a diagnosis.
  • Analyzes and interprets clinical data to identify gaps, inconsistencies, and/or opportunities for improvement in the clinical documentation and queries the provider using concurrent query process following ACDIS/AHIMA Guidelines for a Compliant Query Practice.
  • Acts as a liaison between the Coding Department and Clinical Documentation Integrity to reconcile discrepancies in code and/or DRG assignment.
  • Communicates findings of secondary reviews to Manager.
  • Collaborates with CDI Educator/Auditor when educational needs are identified from second level reviews.
  • Researches, investigates and remains up to date on both clinical and coding guidelines in quarterly Coding Clinics as they relate to physician documentation improvement needed, in an ICD-10 coding environment.
  • Assists in overall quality, timeliness and completeness of the quality health record to ensure appropriate data, provider communication, and quality outcomes. Serves as a resource for appropriate clinical documentation.
  • Documents and tracks second level reviews and results; shares this information with Manager.
  • Collaborates with physicians and/or other clinicians to enhance understanding of the CDI program goals; ensures the medical record can be coded accurately in order to accurately reflect patient severity of illness and risk of mortality.
  • Ensures safe care to patients, staff and visitors; adheres to all Memorial Hermann policies, procedures, and standards within budgetary specifications including time management, supply management, productivity and quality of service.
  • Promotes individual professional growth and development by meeting requirements for mandatory/continuing education and skills competency; supports department-based goals which contribute to the success of the organization; serves as a resource to less experienced staff.
  • Demonstrates commitment to caring for every member of our community by creating compassionate and personalized experiences. Models Memorial Hermann’s service standards of providing safe, caring, personalized and efficient experiences to patients and our workforce.
  • Other duties as assigned.

jobs.excerpt: The Senior Data Engineer, Data Mgmt and BI will design, build, and support scalable data solutions that enable trusted analytics, operational reporting, and data-driven decision making across the organization.
jobs.description:
The Senior Data Engineer, Data Mgmt and BI will design, build, and support scalable data solutions that enable trusted analytics, operational reporting, and data-driven decision making across the organization. This role will partner closely with product, analytics, engineering, and business stakeholders to translate ambiguous business needs into reliable technical solutions, while helping establish strong engineering standards across data pipelines, cloud platforms, data models, APIs, automation, and observability. The ideal candidate is a hands-on engineer who can work independently, mentor others, communicate clearly with technical and non-technical partners, and continuously improve how data is delivered, governed, tested, and supported in a fast-moving environment.

  • Design, build, test, deploy, and maintain scalable data pipelines that ingest, transform, validate, and publish structured and semi-structured data from internal and external sources.
  • Translate business and product requirements into technical designs, data models, integration patterns, and execution plans that support reliable analytics and operational workflows.
  • Develop reusable, maintainable code using modern data engineering practices, with an emphasis on performance, testability, observability, and long-term supportability.
  • Build and optimize batch, event-driven, and serverless data processing patterns using cloud-native services and distributed processing frameworks.
  • Contribute to architecture decisions across data lake, warehouse, orchestration, metadata, API, and application integration patterns.
  • Implement data quality checks, monitoring, alerting, and operational runbooks to ensure pipelines are accurate, reliable, and supportable in production.
  • Design and maintain CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, deployment workflows, and infrastructure-as-code patterns that improve delivery speed and reduce operational risk.
  • Partner with analytics, BI, product, and business teams to enable timely, trusted, and well-documented data products and reporting solutions.
  • Evaluate source systems, APIs, files, data contracts, and transformation logic to identify risks, dependencies, data gaps, and opportunities for simplification.
  • Participate in Agile delivery practices including sprint planning, backlog refinement, code reviews, release planning, incident response, and retrospectives.
  • Mentor engineers, promote engineering best practices, and help raise the quality bar for code, documentation, testing, and production readiness.
  • Create and maintain clear technical documentation, architecture diagrams, data lineage notes, implementation guides, and support materials as systems evolve.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Data Analytics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 5+ years of hands-on data engineering experience designing, building, testing, deploying, and supporting production data pipelines.
  • Strong experience with data modeling, data architecture, ETL/ELT patterns, metadata, data quality, and data warehouse or data lake methodologies.
  • Hands-on experience with cloud data engineering services such as AWS S3, Lambda, Athena, EMR or EMR Serverless, Glue, Step Functions, SNS, SQS, or comparable technologies.
  • Strong programming experience in Scala, Java, SQL, or similar languages used for data processing, automation, and integration.
  • Experience with distributed processing and modern data platforms such as Spark, Databricks, Snowflake, Apache Iceberg, Hive, Redshift, Postgres, SingleStore, or comparable technologies.
