Supports: CityVet and Arista recruiting events (tradeshows, conferences, LP/LVP events, socials, career fairs)

Key Responsibilities

This role runs assigned events from planning through close-out and supports the Senior Manager across the full event portfolio. It is accountable for seven areas of work.

• Event planning & execution. Independently plan and run assigned recruiting events end to end, from registration and show services through shipping, setup, and teardown. Serve as the main contact for show organizers, vendors, and venues on those events.

• Event budget tracking. Build each assigned event's budget from the approved plan, track actuals against it, and flag variances to the Senior Manager early.

• Vendor & contract negotiation. Source vendors and venues, and negotiate pricing and terms within limits the Senior Manager approves. Manage contracts, deposits, invoices, and compliance paperwork.

• Timeline & risk management. Build and keep each event's task board and timeline up to date. Track every show, vendor, and internal deadline, and resolve or escalate risks before they affect the event.

• Team readiness & communication. Prepare onsite teams with travel, credentials, materials, and clear pre-event guidance so everyone arrives ready. Partner with Marketing on collateral and brand standards.

• Onsite leadership. Lead onsite execution at career fairs, socials, and smaller shows. Support the Senior Manager onsite at major national tradeshows.

• Post-event reporting. Close out each event and write the post-event report, including cost, lead, and hire data, with recommendations that feed the Senior Manager's ROI reviews and annual event calendar.

Core Competencies

Success in this role depends on four working habits as much as on event skills.

• Anticipates needs. Sees what each event will need weeks ahead, like a shipping window, a COI, or a badge order, and spots conflicts across events before they surface.

• Leads with recommendations. Brings data-backed options with a clear recommendation (venues, vendors, booth services, budget trade-offs), and carries out the decision once approved.

• Works with a sense of urgency. Moves fast on time-sensitive items like early-bird pricing, vendor holds, and registration cutoffs, and follows up until each one is closed.

• Always meets deadlines. Hits show, vendor, and internal due dates every time across several events running at once. Raises risks early, with a fallback plan already in place.

Qualifications

• 3–5 years of experience in event coordination or event management, including running national tradeshows or conferences. Experience in recruiting, talent acquisition, healthcare, or marketing is a plus.

• Hands-on experience managing exhibitor logistics: booth registration, show services, freight and advance-warehouse shipping, COI/EAC paperwork, and lead retrieval.

• Experience tracking event budgets and negotiating with venues, caterers, A/V, freight, and promotional-item vendors.

• Experience leading onsite event teams and working with leaders and cross-functional partners.

• Highly organized. Able to track dozens of deadlines across several events at once without dropping details.

• Clear, professional written and verbal communication with internal teams, leaders, and outside vendors.

• Proficient with project management tools (monday.com preferred) and Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Excel, Forms, Teams). Experience with CRM/ATS platforms (Gem preferred) is a plus.

• Bachelor's degree in hospitality, event management, marketing, business, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Working Conditions

• Travel up to 10–20% of the time, mostly to national tradeshows, veterinary conferences, and recruiting events, with trips concentrated in peak conference season. Most trips run 2–5 days, including onsite evenings and some weekends for setup, social events, and teardown.

• Ability to support booth setup and teardown, which can include standing for long periods and lifting materials up to 25 lbs.

Caring For You

We know that caring for people and their pets requires energy, empathy, and resilience, so we make it a priority to care for our people by investing in programs, resources, and benefits that support their professional and personal well-being. Eligible Team Members may choose from a range of benefits that help support them and their families through every stage of life.

  • Investment in Your Future. A 401(k) retirement savings plan with a 4% employer match, a Health Savings Account option, and growth opportunities.
  • Work-Life Balance. Enjoy paid time off and floating holidays, flexible schedules, and paid parental leave.
  • Exceptional Health and Supplemental Benefits. Health, Dental (+Adult Ortho option!), Vision, Disability, & Life Insurance, Personal Pet-Care Program, Employee Discount Program.
  • Care When You Need It. We provide free telemedicine for all full-time team members and their families, as well as comprehensive in-the-moment mental health benefits through our robust Employee Assistance Program.

For other CityVet roles, visit our careers page. Follow the growth of CityVet on LinkedIn!

The Toast Enterprise Support team delivers advanced, omnichannel technical support to our most complex enterprise clients — corporate restaurant brands, national franchises, and international locations. As an Enterprise Support Expert, you'll resolve highly complex, high-risk technical issues across a broad and varied product landscape, manage demanding enterprise stakeholders, and bring order to a fast-paced, ambiguous environment — all while fielding incoming questions across phone, chat, and email.

About Cleerly

We’re Cleerly – a healthcare company that’s revolutionizing how heart disease is diagnosed, treated, and tracked. We were founded in 2017 by one of the world’s leading cardiologists and are a growing team. Most of our teams work remotely and have access to our offices in Denver, Colorado, New, York, New York, Dallas, Texas, and Lisbon, Portugal with some roles requiring you to be on-site in a location.

Cleerly has created a new standard of care for heart disease through value-based, AI-driven precision diagnostic solutions with the goal of helping prevent heart attacks. Our technology goes beyond traditional measures of heart disease by enabling comprehensive quantification and characterization of atherosclerosis, or plaque buildup, in each of the heart arteries. Cleerly’s solutions are supported by more than a decade of performing some of the world’s largest clinical trials to identify important findings beyond symptoms that increase a person’s risk of heart attacks.

At Cleerly, we collaborate digitally and use a wide variety of systems. Our people use Google Workspace (GMail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides), Slack, Confluence/Jira, and Zoom Video, prior experience in these areas is a plus. Role or department specific technology needs may vary and will be listed as requirements in the job description.

While we are mostly a remote company, travel is required for some team meetings and cross function projects typically once per month or once per quarter, for some roles like sales or external facing roles travel could be up to 90% of the time.
Cleerly is committed to providing safe and effective medical software that meets customer needs and our intended use. The adherence to all applicable regulatory and statutory requirements establishes a clear framework for setting measurable quality objectives. Our commitment to continually improving our products and processes proactively manages risks, ensuring ongoing compliance throughout the entire software lifecycle. Understanding this role's relevance and importance is critical to achieving Cleerly's quality objectives.

Job Description

We have an immediate opening for a skilled and motivated Support Engineer to join our team. The ideal candidate will be responsible for troubleshooting technical issues, developing tools to aid in issue resolution, trending and reporting areas product fragility and opportunities for enhancement, and collaborating with cross-functional teams to assist in bug identification and fixes.

This role requires a strong technical background, excellent problem-solving and communication skills, and the ability to provide top-tier customer service. You will work closely with our customers and internal teams to ensure the smooth operation of our products and deliver exceptional support in a fast-paced, high-impact healthcare environment.

What would I be doing?

You will be troubleshooting complex problems, creating and maintaining diagnostic tools to streamline the support process, and collaborating with software development teams to assist in bug fixes. Your goal is to ensure timely resolution of issues while providing a positive customer experience. This role will interact with our internal Core Lab team, Engineering, IT, Product Management, Customer Support, Implementation and more. On any given day you could be:

  • Serve as the first point of contact for internal stakeholders to resolve technical issues related to Cleerly products
  • Analyze system logs, software configurations and monitoring tools, and imaging data to diagnose problems
  • Identify, replicate, and document software bugs or malfunctions in collaboration with internal teams
  • Provide prompt and effective assistance via Slack, Zoom, and Jira to our internal teams and occasionally external customers
  • Deliver clear, step-by-step instructions for resolving issues and educating internal users and customers on proper system use
  • Ensure user satisfaction by resolving issues in a timely manner and escalating critical issues when necessary
  • Develop and maintain internal tools and scripts to automate troubleshooting processes and improve overall efficiency
  • Document common issues and solutions to contribute to the internal knowledge base
  • Work closely with software engineers, product development teams, and quality assurance teams to assist in bug fixes and software updates
  • Provide detailed bug reports and insights gathered from customer interactions to aid in product improvement
  • Track, trend, and report potential areas of product fragility or opportunities for product enhancements based on support requests and issues reported
  • Create and update support documentation, user guides, and FAQs

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field
  • 3–5 years of experience in a technical support, application support, or sustaining engineering role, preferably in a healthcare or medical technology environment.
  • Experience with imaging modalities (CT) and related software systems is highly desirable
  • Proficiency with SQL and relational databases (PostgreSQL preferred) for data retrieval and troubleshooting.
  • Familiarity with cloud-based environments (AWS preferred) and cloud monitoring/logging tools (e.g., Datadog, AWS CloudWatch, Lambda) is a strong plus.
  • Familiarity with programming/scripting languages (Python, JavaScript, Bash, Typescript, etc.) to develop troubleshooting tools
  • Comfortable navigating the command line (CLI) and using terminal commands for data manipulation and running scripts.
  • Basic understanding of medical data formats (e.g., DICOM) is a plus.
  • Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal
  • Strong customer service orientation with the ability to manage and de-escalate high-pressure situations
  • Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to think critically and troubleshoot complex issues effectively

The base salary range for this role varies by location and is aligned to market benchmarks.

  • Candidates located in higher-cost labor markets, including California, Washington, New York, New Jersey, Connecticut, Massachusetts, and Washington, DC represent the middle to high end of the range, while candidates located in all other U.S. locations represent the low to middle end of the range.
  • Final compensation is determined based on location, experience, skills, and internal equity.

This role is eligible for a 10% target annual bonus, resulting in the following base salary and Total Target Compensation (TTC) ranges:

  • Base Salary: $85,000 - $99,000

*Total Target Compensation (TTC): Total Cash Compensation (including base pay, variable pay, commission, bonuses, etc.) Additionally, stock options, paid benefits, and employee perks are part of your total rewards.

Working at Cleerly takes HEART. Discover our Core Values:

  • E: Excellence- deliver world-changing results
  • A: Accountability- do what you say; expect the same from others
  • R: Remarkable- inspire & innovate with impact

Riot’s (NASDAQ: RIOT) vision is to be the world’s most trusted platform for powering and building digital infrastructure. We believe that the combination of an innovative spirit and strong community partnership allows us to achieve best-in-class execution and create successful outcomes.

Who we are

At Riot, we’re building the future of digital infrastructure. Our team members have unparalleled opportunities to work on groundbreaking initiatives. Through technical excellence and strategic execution, Riot has positioned itself as a leader in the industry driving advancements that continue to set new benchmarks in digital infrastructure.

We are trailblazers. Problem solvers. People who thrive in fast paced environments, communicate clearly, and bring relentless focus to efficiency and execution.

About the role

RiotPlatforms is building its Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC) function across three pillars: Risk Management, Governance, and Compliance. The team supports contractual commitments for ISO 27001:2022 certification and SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II attestations, as well as Riot’s SOX obligations.

The GRC Program Manager will partner with GRC leaders to build the processes, plans, and reporting needed to coordinate this work across business units and sites. Assigned to the Senior Director or a GRC Director, you will manage initiatives against established deadlines and help maintain audit readiness.

This individual contributor role relies on collaboration and follow-through. You will work across Finance, Legal, IT and Security Engineering, HR, Procurement, and Operations to drive progress and accountability without direct authority.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on program manager who can build processes, navigate GRC requirements, and deliver in a fast-moving environment.

What you'll do

  • Build and improve GRC processes.Partner with GRC leaders to establish the program charter, roles and responsibilities, intake and prioritization processes, meeting cadences, escalation paths, and standards needed to turn GRC strategy into repeatable execution.
  • Drive cross-functional engagement.Lead working groups and coordinate with Finance, Legal, IT and Security Engineering, HR, Procurement, and Operations to integrate GRC requirements into day-to-day work.
  • Manage plans and deadlines.Own the roadmap and schedule for assigned initiatives and help maintain a coordinated enterprise GRC schedule across ISO 27001:2022, SOC 1, SOC 2 Type II, and SOX IT general controls (ITGC).
  • Coordinate certification and audit activities.Work with GRC leaders, control owners, and auditors to track gap remediation, control implementation, evidence readiness, and audit schedules as sites and business units come into scope.
  • Support year-round audit readiness.Help establish and operate consistent processes for evidence ownership, collection, naming, quality review, and retention.
  • Track and report progress.Develop and maintain dashboards and metrics for control-owner timeliness, evidence readiness, remediation aging, policy attestation, and other program priorities. Prepare updates for GRC leadership and the Audit Committee.
  • Deliver assigned GRC initiatives.Work alongside GRC leaders to build and operate processes such as policy review and attestation, remediation and finding tracking, risk management workflows, and control testing schedules.
  • Identify and resolve obstacles.Surface schedule, resource, and control risks early; coordinate follow-up; and escalate issues with options and recommended next steps.
  • Measure program maturity:define and report compliance KPIs such as control-owner timeliness, evidence freshness, remediation aging, and policy attestation rates, and build the executive and Audit Committee dashboards that show progress against target.

What you'll bring

  • 5+ years of program or project management experience, including at least 3 years managing GRC, IT audit, security compliance, or risk initiatives.
  • Experience supporting GRC, compliance, or related programs in a data center, colocation, or critical infrastructure environment, such as energy, utilities, or digital asset mining.
  • Hands-on ownership of the program plan and timeline for at least one ISO 27001 certification or SOC 1 or SOC 2 Type II audit cycle—not solely evidence collection.
  • Working knowledge of ISO 27001:2022, SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria, SOX IT general controls (ITGC), and NIST CSF, with the ability to translate control requirements into actionable plans.
  • A track record of delivering complex, cross-functional programs against certification, regulatory, or contractual deadlines, with measurable results.
  • Experience preparing clear, accurate reporting for executive leadership.
  • Proven ability to coordinate work and drive accountability across teams without direct authority.
  • Experience building or establishing processes in a fast-moving environment.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, including status reporting that distinguishes planned, in progress, complete, and verified work.
  • Experience using GRC platforms, such as Vanta, Drata, Hyperproof, ServiceNow GRC/IRM, or OneTrust, and work management tools, such as Asana, Jira, or Smartsheet.

Preferred:

  • Relevant certifications:PMP, PgMP, or equivalent project management credential. GRC-specific credentials—such as ISO 27001 Lead Implementer, ISO 27001 Lead Auditor, CISA, or CRISC—are strongly valued.
  • Public company audit coordination:Proven experience operating in a publicly traded company, collaborating directly with Internal Audit and independent external audit firms.
  • Greenfield program build:Demonstrated experience standing up a GRC PMO, operating model, or cross-functional delivery cadences from scratch.
  • Executive and committee reporting:Familiarity with preparing status reports, risk summaries, or presentation materials for executive leadership and the Audit Committee.

Compensation and Benefits

  • Wellness & Lifestyle Perks: Enjoy free gym memberships, pet insurance, childcare discounts, and more to support your life both in and out of work.

jobs.excerpt: CrossCountry Consulting is the transformation partner for the Office of the CFO.
jobs.description:
CrossCountry Consulting is the transformation partner for the Office of the CFO. As a trusted advisor to Fortune 500 companies, emerging growth market leaders, and private equity sponsors, we combine deep domain expertise with the power of data, AI, and technology to modernize workflows, drive human-centered change, and maximize transaction value. Grounded in our Core Values, we are committed to solving today's most complex challenges while delivering a better experience for our clients, our people, and our communities. When you join CrossCountry, you become part of a team that believes in collaboration, generosity, and the drive to help our clients work smarter, build resiliency, and prepare for the future.

Role Overview

    The Business Applications End-to-End Architect is accountable for one outcome: a portfolio company’s systems working together in production, in service of the business. On PE-backed programs, CRM, CPQ, ERP, billing, revenue recognition, EPM, the data warehouse, and integration layers are usually delivered by different vendors or teams. Each can report that its own piece is healthy while the program still fails at the seams. This role owns the seams.

    You design and deliver the full flow from CRM through billing, revenue, and the ERP into the data warehouse and EPM tools, so the business operates, closes, and reports from one trusted set of numbers. You also orchestrate the program around that architecture, owning the plan, milestones, dependencies, and critical path, with a PMO or program administrator supporting you on complex programs.

    Your work is measured by a working, integrated landscape, not by roadmaps or presentations. Where an iPaaS architect (Boomi, Celigo, or similar) keeps integration flows stable, you decide how data and transactions move across every system and prove the whole landscape works for the CFO, the CRO, the Controller, and the PE sponsor.

    Good architecture depends on an operator view: how deals are booked, customers are billed, revenue is recognized, the month-end close runs, and who owns the system after the consultants leave.

    If you want to advise from the sidelines, this is not the role. If you want to see the full picture, from the first CRM opportunity to the board-level report, and be accountable for it working, this is.

What Success Looks Like:

    Success in this role is measured by outcomes in production: systems that work together, numbers that tie, and a business that runs on what was built. Strong recommendations and clear communication matter, and they are the means to that end. In practice, success looks like:

  • Systems go live on the committed plan, and the go/no-go decision was made on objective criteria and proved to be the right call
  • Data reconciles across CRM, billing, revenue, the ERP, and the data warehouse, and the numbers hold up under scrutiny from the Controller, the auditors, and the sponsor
  • The month-end close runs on the new landscape without workarounds that were visible before go-live
  • Integration, data migration, and cutover risks are surfaced and resolved weeks before they threaten the date, not discovered at the end
  • Vendors and internal teams build to a design that serves the business outcome, and gaps between them are caught by you first
  • The client team can operate and own the landscape after hypercare

What You'll Do:

    Design and deliver the architecture

  • Design the future-state application landscape across CRM, CPQ, ERP, billing, revenue recognition, EPM, data warehouse, and integration platforms, without bias toward any single technology
  • Define system-of-record decisions and data ownership at each step of lead-to-cash, quote-to-cash, procure-to-pay, record-to-report, and planning and reporting
  • Write the design documentation (integration designs, data flows, and mapping decisions) that implementation teams and vendors build against
  • Review and challenge vendor and integration partner designs to confirm they serve the business outcome, not just the component in scope
  • Validate the build through testing: define end-to-end test scenarios, run integrated testing and UAT, and drive defects to resolution across systems and vendors
  • Own data migration strategy, reconciliation, and cutover planning, including the go-live readiness scorecard and go/no-go recommendation
  • Diagnose and resolve cross-system issues when numbers do not tie, integrations fail, or processes break after go-live
  • Identify where AI capabilities within the stack can add practical value (such as data validation, reconciliation, anomaly detection, and workflow automation), and design the data foundations and controls they require

    • Orchestrate the program

  • Build and own the integrated program plan across workstreams and vendors, defining milestones, cross-system dependencies, and the critical path
  • Run dependency, risk, and issue management across CRM, ERP, billing and revenue, integration, data, and reporting workstreams, and escalate early to the CCC Partner when issues exceed program-level authority
  • Direct a PMO or program administrator on complex programs, who runs day-to-day plan maintenance, RAID logs, status reporting, and meeting cadence against the plan you set
  • Use AI-assisted tooling to strengthen orchestration (scenario planning, dependency tracking, status synthesis), with human judgment retained on decisions

    • Lead the stakeholders

  • Lead design workshops and working sessions that end in decisions, and bridge business leaders (CFO, Controller, CRO or Head of Sales Operations, FP&A) and technical teams (ERP developers, integration architects, Salesforce architects, data engineers)
  • Give PE sponsors and portfolio company leadership direct, data-backed status and risk communication, particularly under timeline pressure
  • Coordinate with CrossCountry service lines, including our Salesforce practice, and third-party vendors under one program governance model
  • Support business development by contributing to scoping and solution design, including early involvement on multi-service-line or multi-vendor opportunities before statements of work are finalized

What You'll Bring:

    Core (the hardest requirements to teach)

  • Operator view: A demonstrated understanding of how a business runs day to day, including what a close looks like, how revenue is booked and billed, what breaks when a system change meets real volume, and what an organization can realistically absorb and sustain. This can come from in-house roles, deep embedded work with operating teams, or both
  • End-to-end delivery ownership: At least one major ERP implementation or multi-system program delivered through go-live and hypercare in a lead capacity (not solely as a workstream lead), with direct accountability for integration, data migration, and cutover. You should be able to describe a multi-system go-live you owned, what broke, and what you did about it
  • ERP depth: Deep hands-on experience with at least one major ERP platform (for example NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Oracle Cloud, SAP, or Oracle EBS), with the ability to advise credibly across platforms
  • CRM depth: Strong working knowledge of Salesforce and CRM architecture (for example Sales Cloud, CPQ, Revenue Cloud, or similar), including opportunity-to-quote-to-order design, product and pricing structure, and how CRM data feeds billing, revenue, and finance. You do not need to be a Salesforce developer, but you must be able to hold a credible design conversation with Salesforce architects and the sales organization

    • Required domain and context

  • Experience designing or advising on billing and revenue recognition architecture (usage, subscription, and complex contract billing), with knowledge of platforms such as Zuora Revenue, Zone Billing, or similar, and of ASC 606 implications for system design
  • Experience designing or advising on integrations across CRM, CPQ, ERP, billing, and revenue systems, with working knowledge of integration patterns (point-to-point vs. middleware, real-time vs. batch)
  • Experience in PE-backed or high-growth environments where speed, pragmatism, and value creation drive decisions
  • Experience supporting M&A integration or carve-out engagements
  • Practical capability applying AI to the business application stack: understanding what AI features within CRM, ERP, billing, EPM, and data platforms can and cannot do today, and what data quality, security, and control foundations they require. The emphasis is on making the existing stack smarter and more efficient, not on building standalone AI solutions

    • Required working knowledge (with room to grow)

  • EPM and planning platforms (for example NetSuite Planning and Budgeting, Oracle EPM, Anaplan, Adaptive) and how they connect to ERP actuals
  • Data warehouse and analytics architecture (for example Snowflake or similar cloud data platforms, with BI and reporting layers) and how financial and operational data is modeled and reconciled across systems

Qualifications:

    Required:

  • 8+ years of experience in enterprise technology architecture, ERP implementation, or finance systems transformation

jobs.excerpt: About WRS HealthWRS Health builds an Electronic Health Records (EHR) system that medical practices rely on every day to care for patients.
jobs.description:
About WRS Health

WRS Health builds an Electronic Health Records (EHR) system that medical practices rely on every day to care for patients. Our platform runs on Linux servers in AWS with a PHP application stack, and it holds some of the most sensitive data there is: protected health information.
We are now investing heavily in AI agents that work alongside clinicians and staff. That shift opens new ground for our product and new attack surfaces for our security program. We are hiring a Security Engineer to help us protect both.

The role

As our Security Engineer, you will find and fix security risks before attackers do, across our AWS infrastructure, our PHP application, and our growing fleet of AI agents. You will look ahead to emerging threats, especially those unique to LLMs and autonomous agents, and build defenses before they are needed.
This is a hands-on, collaborative role. You will work directly with our development and AI teams, helping them understand issues, prioritize fixes, and ship secure code. We want someone who teaches and enables, not someone who only files tickets.

What you'll do

Application security
  • Review PHP code and architecture for vulnerabilities such as injection, broken authentication, insecure deserialization, and access-control flaws.
  • Run and tune SAST, DAST, and dependency scanning (e.g., Composer packages) in our CI/CD pipelines.
  • Lead threat modeling for new features and work with developers to fix findings, with clear guidance and secure code examples.
Cloud and infrastructure security
  • Harden our AWS environment: IAM least privilege, network segmentation, encryption at rest and in transit, and secrets management.
  • Monitor and respond to findings from tools such as GuardDuty, Security Hub, CloudTrail, and AWS Config.
  • Secure and patch Linux servers, and define hardened baselines for new infrastructure.
AI and agent security
  • Assess AI agents for risks such as prompt injection, data leakage, excessive permissions, insecure tool use, and model supply-chain issues.
  • Define guardrails for what agents can access and do, especially where PHI is involved, including logging, human-in-the-loop controls, and output validation.
  • Partner with the AI team to build security into agent design from the start, using frameworks such as the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications.
Threat management and response
  • Track emerging threats to healthcare, cloud, and AI systems, and turn that intelligence into concrete defenses.
  • Coordinate penetration tests and vulnerability management, from discovery through verified fix.
  • Help build and run our incident response plan, including tabletop exercises.
Compliance and culture
  • Support HIPAA and HITECH compliance.
  • Run secure-coding training and build security awareness across engineering.

Qualifications

  • 4+ years in security engineering, application security, or a closely related role.
  • Hands-on experience securing AWS environments, including IAM, VPC design, KMS, and AWS security services.
  • Strong Linux administration and hardening skills.
  • Experience with vulnerability scanning, penetration testing, and driving findings to resolution.
  • Working knowledge of LLM and AI agent risks, such as prompt injection, data exfiltration through tools, and over-permissioned agents.
  • Scripting or automation skills in Python, Bash, or similar.
  • Clear communication, and the ability to explain risk to developers and leadership in practical terms.
  • Familiarity with HIPAA or other regulated-data environments.

Nice to have

  • Experience in healthcare IT or with EHR systems and standards such as HL7 or FHIR.
  • Prior work securing AI agents, RAG pipelines, or LLM integrations in production.
  • Infrastructure-as-code security (Terraform or CloudFormation) and container security.

What success looks like in your first year

  1. First 90 days: You have assessed our AWS, Linux, and PHP environments and our AI agent designs, and you have a prioritized risk roadmap.
  2. By six months: Automated security scanning runs in every pipeline, and developers fix critical findings quickly with your guidance.
  3. By one year: Every new AI agent passes a security review before launch, our incident response plan has been tested, and security is part of how engineering works day to day.

Details and how to apply

  • Location: Remote
  • Employment type: Full-time - Independent Contractor
  • Reports to: CTO
  • Hours: Must be available during standard US business hours (9:00 AM – 5:00 PM EST or 8:30 AM – 4:30 PM EST)

WRS Health is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic.

Our growing team is looking for an Engineering Manager to help take our web application, services, and agentic development practices to the next level.This role leads a cluster of small, cross-functional fusion pods that use AI agentic development across the SDLC. You will create the conditions for the pod to deliver customer value quickly, safely, and predictably while preserving strong technical judgment, product quality, and team health.The right leader is a technically credible people manager who can efficiently operate across multiple work-streams. You will partner closely with Product Management, Architecture, Platform, Security, and other engineering leaders to clarify outcomes, remove dependencies, improve engineering effectiveness, and develop the next generation of leaders.

What You’ll Do:

  • Lead and develop a cluster of three to four Fusion Pods, establishing clear charters, ownership boundaries, operating rhythms, and escalation paths.
  • Partner with Product Management and other stakeholders to translate customer and business outcomes into priorities, delivery commitments, dependency plans, and risk decisions.
  • Own people leadership for the cluster, including one-on-ones, feedback, performance and career development, recognition, hiring, onboarding, retention, and development of future pod and technical leaders.
  • Maintain delivery visibility across the cluster, remove blockers, communicate changes transparently, lead overall release management and represent the pods in planning, roadmap, hiring, and cross-functional leadership forums.
  • Engineering technical leadership - Guide technical quality through architecture and design reviews, technical planning, code reviews, and production-readiness discussions while preserving pod ownership of day-to-day decisions by collaborating with VP of Product Development.
  • Establish and track expectations for AI-agent use, context repository, reusable skills, workflow quality, review practices, secure tool usage, and human accountability.
  • Ensure consistent practices for testing, security, performance, reliability, observability, documentation, and incident follow-through across the pods.
  • Use delivery, quality, reliability, pod experience, and customer-impact signals to improve the operating model, reduce duplicated work, and prioritize shared technical investments.

Your First 90 Days:

By Day 30

  • With the support of your leadership team, you will participate in our virtual immersive onboarding program to learn our product, customers, organization, and technology stack.
  • You will meet the fusion pods, product partners, architecture and platform partners, and key stakeholders. You will understand each pod’s charter, roadmap, dependencies, production responsibilities, team-health signals, and current use of AI-assisted development tools.
  • You will observe pod ceremonies, design and code reviews, release and incident practices, and identify the most important opportunities and risks across the cluster.

By Day 60

  • You will work with the pod teams and product management to clarify ownership, delivery priorities, technical risks, and cross-pod dependencies.
  • You will establish a lightweight operating rhythm for the cluster, including delivery reviews, dependency management, people-leadership routines, and a consistent approach to surfacing risks and decisions.
  • You will partner with technical leads and senior team members to identify improvements to AI-assisted development workflows, quality practices, developer experience, and production readiness.

By Day 90

  • You will play an integral role in delivering roadmap commitments across the Fusion Pod cluster.
  • You will have established clear expectations for pod ownership, delivery accountability, technical leadership, and team health. You will have a prioritized improvement plan with measurable outcomes and will have begun executing the highest-value changes.
  • You will contribute to hiring and development plans, strengthen cross-pod collaboration, and help the teams adopt AI-assisted practices that improve speed and quality without weakening engineering judgment or accountability.

Who You Are:

  • 8+ years of software engineering experience in an enterprise SaaS product-development environment.
  • 5+ years of experience directly managing software engineers and leading engineering teams.
  • Experience leading multiple teams, pods, workstreams, or product areas concurrently.
  • Strong technical depth in distributed systems, web applications, APIs, data-intensive services, cloud platforms, or comparable product technology.
  • The ability to participate meaningfully in architecture, design, code-quality, reliability, and production-readiness discussions.
  • Experience partnering with Product Management and other stakeholders to plan, prioritize, estimate, sequence, and deliver customer-facing software.
  • Experience building healthy teams through coaching, feedback, career development, hiring, onboarding, and performance management.
  • Experience working in a HyperAgile or Agile environment
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate risks, trade-offs, decisions, and changes clearly.
  • A track record of improving delivery predictability, quality, reliability, developer experience, or engineering effectiveness.

Your Differentiators:

  • Experience leading or championing AI-assisted or agentic development practices across an engineering team or organization.
  • Practical experience with tools such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, or comparable agentic development tools.
  • Experience establishing standards for AI-generated code review, testing, evaluation, observability, secure tool access, and human accountability.
  • Experience building or operating shared developer platforms, reusable engineering workflows, internal tooling, or engineering enablement programs.
  • Experience leading a transition from larger Scrum teams to smaller, outcome-oriented pods.
  • Experience with Java, full-stack web development, relational databases, RESTful APIs, cloud services, CI/CD, Docker, and modern front-end frameworks.
  • Experience in regulated industry environments where security, auditability, reliability, and customer trust are essential.

Our Values

  • We are a Team. Employees, customers, and partners working together.
  • We are Customer-Focused. Customers are the heart of everything we do.
  • We are Driven. Seeking exceptional outcomes.
  • We Own our Success. Every employee has a stake in our company.
  • We do the right thing and have fun in the process.

As a member of the World Wide Strategic Accounts field team, the Cloud Native Architect (CNA) is a senior technologist who owns the technical sales strategy, evaluation program, and architectural vision creating repeatable business with software opportunities with the company’s largest multinational customers. You will guide C‑level and engineering stakeholders through solution discovery, validation, and financial justification, ensuring every engagement results in a technical win and a clear path to enterprise‑wide adoption that delivers the customers business outcomes aligned to the project. Driving Everpure as the standard solution for delivering data-management in the WWSA Segment. Creating market penetration strategy and thought leadership across the entire theater/segment.

The role of a Cloud Native Architect (CNA) is a multifaceted position that serves as a technical bridge between the sales, product, and engineering teams. This role is important for driving revenue growth and enhancing customer relationships by providing technical solutions for a specific set of accounts. Primarily focused on the pre-sales process, the individual in this role will engage with potential and existing customers to understand their business issues and technical hurdles related to Kubernetes. They will deliver tailored product demonstrations, respond to technical inquiries, and work with the Everpure technical field to architect solutions that integrate Everpure offerings with clients' software driven platforms. The responsibilities of the Cloud Native Architect will fall into (5) categories:

  • Technical Qualification
  • Solution Validation
  • Prospect to Customer Transition
  • Established Customer Satisfaction

These categories will serve not only as the foundation for the role, but align with the Technical Sales Process to provide the best possible customer experience.

jobs.description:
We're Hiring

Remote Academic Coach & Student Assistant (Part-Time, ~10 hours/week)

The steady partner who helps a high-achieving student master hard material and never miss a deadline.

About the Role

Seamless Assist is hiring a part-time Academic Coach & Student Assistant for a US-based family. You will work one-on-one, online, with their daughter, a motivated high-school student taking classes a year ahead of her grade, including several college-level Advanced Placement (AP) courses. This role reports to the student's parent.

Why This Role Exists

The student doesn't need to be taught from scratch. She is carrying a demanding, writing-heavy course load, and the pressure is in the volume: essays, problem sets, labs, tests and extracurricular deadlines all landing in the same week. This role exists to give her a sharp, organised partner who can keep up with advanced material, help her work through the hardest parts, and keep her schedule under control so nothing slips.

Her Current Classes

  • AP Microeconomics & Macroeconomics
  • AP Biology
  • AP English Language & Composition
  • AP US History
  • Pre-Calculus
  • Spanish 4
  • Journalism & News Production

You don't need to be an expert in every subject. You do need to be strong in several of them, especially writing-heavy courses (AP English Language, AP US History) and at least one of economics, biology or maths.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

Academic coaching (about 70% of your time)

  • Run live one-on-one video sessions to work through homework, problem sets, essays and test preparation.
  • Explain difficult concepts clearly and check that she can explain them back.
  • Review essays and written work for argument, structure, evidence and citations, including AP-style timed essays.
  • Build practice questions, review plans and study guides ahead of tests and the AP exams in May.
  • Learn how each course is taught and graded (syllabi, teacher rubrics, the College Board AP course frameworks) and coach to them.
  • Coach, never complete. Her work must always be her own, in line with her school's academic integrity rules.

Planning and student assistant support (about 30% of your time)

  • Run a weekly planning session: map every class's assignments, tests and deadlines into a shared calendar and task list.
  • Keep her schedule current across classes, activities and appointments, with study time blocked in.
  • Send short reminders before deadlines and confirm work was actually submitted.
  • Track grades and flag early when something starts to slip.
  • Send the parent a short weekly progress update.

Schedule

About 10 hours per week. Sessions fall on weekday afternoons and evenings, US Pacific Time (roughly 3:30–8:30 pm PT), plus one short weekend planning session. You must be reliably available in that window.

Who Will Succeed in This Role

This is a high-trust role with a bright, busy teenager. You will need real subject depth, patience, and the organisational discipline of a strong executive assistant.

  • You explain things clearly and can tell the difference between "I get it" and actually getting it.
  • You are a strong writer and can give specific, useful feedback on an argumentative essay.
  • You run your own life from a calendar and a task list, and you follow up without being asked.
  • You are warm, steady and encouraging, and you hold a high standard.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree or higher, ideally in education, English, history, economics, biology, mathematics or a related field.
  • At least 2 years of tutoring or teaching high-school or first-year university students.
  • Strong command of the material in several of the subjects listed above.
  • Excellent written and spoken English. Your writing will be assessed during screening.
  • Uses AI tools in your daily work (for example Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini) to build study materials and plan faster, and can teach a student to use them responsibly and within school rules.
  • Able to work US Pacific Time afternoons and evenings, about 10 hours per week.
  • Reliable high-speed internet, a quiet workspace, a webcam and a backup power or internet plan.
  • Willing to complete a national police clearance or background check and provide two professional references before starting.

Nice to have

  • Experience with the US Advanced Placement (AP) programme, or strong AP, SAT, IB or A-Level results of your own.
  • Conversational or better Spanish.
  • Journalism, editing or newsroom experience.
  • Comfortable in Google Workspace (Calendar, Docs, Drive) and a task tool such as Notion or Todoist.

How We Work

Because this role involves working one-on-one with a teenager, clear safeguards apply. All sessions run on a family-owned video account and are recorded. All messages go through a group channel that includes a parent. There is no private messaging or social-media contact with the student. A background check and references are required before the first paid session.

Pay

Competitive hourly pay, paid monthly in USD. Pay varies by country.

How to Apply

Apply with your CV. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to a short AI-led video interview, a written subject task, an interview with the family and a paid trial session.

jobs.excerpt: Who we are At Twilio, we’re shaping the future of communications, all from the comfort of our homes.
jobs.description:
Who we are

At Twilio, we’re shaping the future of communications, all from the comfort of our homes. We deliver innovative solutions to hundreds of thousands of businesses and empower millions of developers worldwide to craft personalized customer experiences.

Our dedication to remote-first work, and strong culture of connection and global inclusion means that no matter your location, you’re part of a vibrant team with diverse experiences making a global impact each day. As we continue to revolutionize how the world interacts, we’re acquiring new skills and experiences that make work feel truly rewarding. Your career at Twilio is in your hands.

.

Hiring and how we work

We use Artificial Intelligence (AI) to help make our hiring process efficient. That said, every hiring decision is made by real Twilions!

Also, while we are a remote-first company, you may be asked to report in person on an ad-hoc basis for team gatherings, functional off-sites or customer meetings.

.

See yourself at Twilio

Join the team as Twilio’s next Developer Evangelist.

About the job

This position is needed to help us inspire and equip a global network of millions of developers who will build the future of customer engagement. The Developer Evangelist specializing in AI technology will define developer relations and build the AI community in the Bay Area, while sustaining a relationship that fuels every developer's journey to know, use and love Twilio. The Developer Evangelist will serve as the regional liaison for local developer communities, build Twilio-powered solutions, such as SMS, Voice and Email, to address developer needs and partner with Marketing, Product and additional cross-functional teams. The role requires an understanding of the AI developer community and technical knowledge, as well as the ability to take complex ideas and make them accessible in order to inspire creativity through code.

Responsibilities

In this role, you’ll:

  • Help us inspire and equip developers to build with Twilio products and AI technology, ensuring an exceptional developer experience with Twilio.
  • Be an active and authentic participant in the developer community wherever they gather online and offline. For many of those developers, you will be "the face" of Twilio -- the person they ping when they need help. They will feel like VIPs because they know you. And when someone who works at Twilio needs to talk to developers in the Bay Area and North America developer community, they'll come to you.
  • Attend, plan and speak at in-person and virtual events.
  • Write clear and empathetic content that breaks down the complex into the understandable while telling stories with code, equipping developers with knowledge of tools and techniques.
  • Navigate cross-functional collaboration and partner within Twilio to align with program and engagement objectives.
  • Drive projects independently from inception to completion, outlining key milestones and ensuring deadlines are met.
  • Communicate project plans, progress, and outcomes effectively to stakeholders at all levels within the region and across the company.

Qualifications

Twilio values diverse experiences from all kinds of industries, and we encourage everyone who meets the required qualifications to apply. If your career is just starting or hasn't followed a traditional path, don't let that stop you from considering Twilio. We are always looking for people who will bring something new to the table!

*Required:

  • Proficient in writing Python, PHP, Node, C# (.NET), or Java with insights into web frameworks within or across these languages.
  • Technical foundational expertise in AI tools, technologies and/or platforms.
  • Ability to navigate the emerging AI developer ecosystem, community and emerging industry trends.
  • A love of teaching others, curiosity and excitement about technology.
  • 3-5 years of experience writing production code, with strong empathy for developers to successfully guide their building process.
  • Experience in cross-functional collaboration with teams like sales, support, product and marketing.
  • Creative and collaborative problem-solving skills, with a focus on data-driven decision-making for system and process improvements.
  • Skilled in storytelling to highlight developers building on Twilio and inspire others.
  • Experience in public speaking, writing, and/or organizing engaging programs.

Desired:

  • Familiarity with the Bay Area developer community and industry landscape, including local communities, events and programs.
  • Familiarity with the local AI developer ecosystem, particularly through the Developer Relations lens.
  • Familiarity with project management tools and methodologies.
  • Ability to influence and build effective working relationships across all levels of the organization.
  • Excellent skills in influencing, problem-solving, consensus-building, and strong interpersonal communication.
  • Experience in organizing and running developer events, meetups and/or user groups

Location

This role will be remote and based in the Bay Area.

Travel

We prioritize connection and opportunities to build relationships with our customers and each other. For this role, approximately travel is anticipated to help you connect in-person in a meaningful way.

What We Offer

Working at Twilio offers many benefits, including competitive pay, generous time off, ample parental and wellness leave, healthcare, a retirement savings program, and much more. Offerings vary by location.

Compensation

The estimated pay ranges for this role are as follows:

  • Based in Colorado, Hawaii, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Vermont or Washington D.C. : $131,440 - $164,300.
  • Based in New York, New Jersey, Washington State, or California (outside of the San Francisco Bay area): $139,200 - $174,000.
  • Based in the San Francisco Bay area, California: $154,640 - $193,300.
  • This role may be eligible to participate in Twilio’s equity plan and corporate bonus plan. All roles are generally eligible for the following benefits: health care insurance, 401(k) retirement account, paid sick time, paid personal time off, paid parental leave.

The successful candidate’s starting salary will be determined based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location.

Application deadline information

Applications for this role are intended to be accepted until November 30, 2026, but may change based on business needs.

Twilio thinks big. Do you?

We like to solve problems, take initiative, pitch in when needed, and are always up for trying new things. That's why we seek out colleagues who embody our values — something we call Twilio Magic. Additionally, we empower employees to build positive change in their communities by supporting their volunteering and donation efforts.

So, if you're ready to unleash your full potential, do your best work, and be the best version of yourself, apply now! If this role isn't what you're looking for, please consider other open positions.

jobs.title: Engineering Manager
jobs.excerpt: We are hiring an Engineering Manager to lead the Data Platform team, the group that builds the data foundation every other part of Istari depends on.
jobs.description:
We are hiring an Engineering Manager to lead the Data Platform team, the group that builds the data foundation every other part of Istari depends on. That foundation covers how engineering models and their metadata are registered, versioned, related, queried, and traced across customer environments, and how AI agents get safe, governed access to that data. Istari is doing groundbreaking work in the area of digital threading, branching and merging, global collision-free namespacing and tracing with hashes, digital signatures, Merkle trees, and other advanced technologies to build an “internet of engineering data” (also broadly applicable to any kind of structured and semi-structured data).

Istari is also the owner/upstream on the well-known and well-respected distributed graph database . In this role you will supervise and guide a team of engineers who develop and lead the Dgraph open source community, and provide additional capabilities and support to enterprise customers of Dgraph.

This is a player-coach-friendly role on a small, senior team. You will manage engineers, own delivery and technical quality for the team's roadmap, and partner closely with Product, Security, Infrastructure, and Customer Engineering. This role reports to our CTO, and we are looking for someone who has built data systems under real constraints (scale, security, uptime) and who likes growing a team while delivering high quality software at a rapid pace.

Core Responsibilities:

    Lead and grow the team

  • Hire, onboard, coach, and retain strong data and backend engineers; run 1:1s, feedback, and promotion cycles.

  • Set clear priorities and expectations, and build a culture of ownership, code review, and honest postmortems.

  • Stay close enough to the code to review designs and unblock the team, without becoming the bottleneck.

  • Work with other engineering teams at Istari to coordinate frequent releases using DevSecOps processes.

  • Optimize the components you own to support the broader Istari platform roadmap and lifecycle.

    • Deliver the data platform roadmap

  • Turn product and customer needs into a roadmap, then plan, scope, and ship it with the team.

  • Own the data layer behind the Istari platform: metadata and file registration, versioning, lineage and traceability, graph-based relationships, and APIs for query and ingestion.

  • Make pragmatic build-versus-buy and architecture calls, and keep quality, reliability, and cost under control.

    • Build for regulated, high-assurance environments

  • Design for data sovereignty: data stays in customer-controlled storage and environments, and the platform works across security levels and deployment models (cloud-hosted and customer-hosted).

  • Work with Security and DevSecOps on access control, auditability, and compliance readiness.

  • Define SLOs and on-call practices, and lead incident response and follow-up for the data tier.

    • Enable AI and agentic workflows

  • Partner with Product and AI engineers so agents and models get governed, safe, and monitored access to engineering data maintained by the Istari platform.

  • Help shape how we represent engineering data (models, requirements, simulation results) so it is queryable and trustworthy for both humans and their AI agents; help design safeguards against AI-induced errors or hallucinations.

    • Build with AI and AI agents

  • Lean in to the latest AI technologies in order to optimize code delivery without sacrificing quality, and guide your team in doing so as well.

  • Focus on automation across the product lifecycle and all engineering processes with the right safeguards, including adversarial AI usage and appropriate human-in-the-loop oversight.

    • Work across the company

  • Collaborate with Product, Customer Engineering, and Solutions on customer deployments, integrations, and escalations.

  • Communicate plans, risks, and tradeoffs clearly to leadership and technical customers.

Required Qualifications:

  • 7+ years of software product engineering experience, including 2+ years managing engineers (or leading teams as a tech lead with formal people-management responsibility).

  • Hands-on background building and operating data-intensive backend systems: databases (notably Postgres), data pipelines, metadata or catalog systems, blockchain systems, or storage services in production.

  • Solid grounding in data modeling and at least one of: graph databases, relational databases at scale, or distributed data stores. You can review a schema or a query plan and have an expert opinion.

  • Experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS preferred), containers, and Kubernetes, and with CI/CD and observability practices.

  • Track record of hiring well, developing engineers, and delivering on a roadmap in a small, fast-moving team.

  • Clear communication with technical and non-technical stakeholders, including customers.

  • Comfort with ambiguity: you can set direction when requirements are still forming and adjust as we learn.

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, or equivalent practical experience.

    • Nice to Have

  • Experience with Dgraph, GraphQL, or knowledge-graph and ontology design.

  • Background in aerospace, defense, or other regulated industries, or with model-based systems engineering (MBSE) and digital engineering tools such as CAD, simulation, or SysML.

  • Experience with data governance, lineage, access control, or air-gapped and customer-hosted deployments.

  • Familiarity with FedRAMP, NIST 800-53, CMMC, or similar compliance frameworks.

  • Exposure to building data foundations for ML or AI agents, such as retrieval, RAG, vector search, or agent tool access.

  • Prior experience at an early-stage or defense-tech startup.

  • Active U.S. security clearance, or the ability to obtain one.

What Success Looks Like

    First 90 days

  • You know the team, the codebase, and our customers' data problems well enough to explain them to a new hire.

  • You have 1:1 rhythms, clear priorities, and a shared view of team health and delivery.

  • You have shipped or unblocked at least one meaningful platform improvement.

    • First 6 months

  • The team has a written roadmap tied to customer outcomes, with owners, milestones, and reliability targets.

  • Open roles are filled or in late-stage interviews, and every engineer has a growth plan.

  • Incident response and on-call for the data tier are predictable and documented.

    • First 12 months

  • The data platform scales to our largest customer deployments and meets our security and compliance bar.

  • The Istari data fabric (Postgres, Dgraph, ElasticSearch/OpenSearch, S3, etc.) work as one product that Product and AI teams build on with confidence.

  • The team is known across the company as dependable, and people want to join it.

About Istari Digital

    Istari is a digital engineering software company building open, scalable infrastructure for engineering data. Our platform lets customers simply and securely integrate engineering models across disciplines, organizations, and security levels — whether they're designing prototypes, performing virtual testing, or training AI and autonomy for complex systems.

    Focus is rewarded. Finish is remembered.

    Facts are friendly. Even when they are not fun.

    Fellowship is fundamental. Make others successful.

Who We Are

We come for the impact, and stay for the culture! We’re a talented, opinionated, passionate, fiercely inclusive, and responsible group of bees. We have conviction and we strive to live our values every day. We want our people to do what they truly love amongst a team of highly talented (but humble) peers.

How We Work

We are a fully distributed company, which means we believe it is not where you sit, but how you deliver that matters most. We invest in our people and care about how you orient to our culture and processes. At the same time we imbue a lot of trust, autonomy, and accountability from Day 1.

Little more about the team:

AI agents at Honeycomb investigate, reason, and act on real observability data. They live in Canvas: the agentic workspace where engineers go to understand their systems.

The Agentic Intelligence team has shipped Canvas, the Honeycomb MCP server, and the Canvas Agent and Canvas Skills surfaces. What we're looking for today is someone who brings deep agent expertise and uses it to expand what the team can build: new agents, new surface area in Canvas, memory, spatial awareness, improved performance on our Bedrock loop.

Honeycomb's data store is fast and accepts high cardinality data; that's what makes agents built on top of it different from anything built on a conventional observability backend. This role is about taking advantage of that building agents that can do things no other observability product can do because the underlying data makes it possible.

Some of this work will start as a prototype. The expectation is that the code makes it through the full arc, from the rough first version through to something that holds up in production.

jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

Please note this is an evergreen position. We accept applications on an ongoing basis to build a talent pipeline for roles that open regularly. Because this posting may not reflect a current opening, we may not contact every applicant. If your background aligns with an open need, our team will reach out. We also encourage you to visit our careers page to explore other opportunities.


BACKGROUND: Founded in 1933, the International Rescue Committee is a leading, non-sectarian, non-profit organization providing emergency relief, protection, rehabilitation assistance, resettlement services, and advocacy for refugees and victims of oppression or violent conflict. Domestically, our 26 offices across the U.S. ensure new arrivals have food, shelter, and clothing, and work with refugees to help them gain self-sufficiency.

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is one of the leading providers of high-quality programming for refugees resettling to the United States. The IRC is committed to developing innovative programs that respond to the refugees’ unique strengths and needs, using our learning and experience to shape policy and practice, and highlighting and promoting best practices in refugee services provision.

Switchboard is a one-stop resource hub for refugee service providers in the United States. Switchboard provides training and capacity-building services to service providers in the United States, including resettlement agencies and affiliates, state agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others. More information about Switchboard can be found at www.SwitchboardTA.org.

SCOPE OF INTERN WORK: With guidance and mentorship from the Switchboard training team, the intern will contribute to the development and delivery of engaging training and technical assistance resources that strengthen the knowledge and skills of resettlement service providers. The intern will have opportunities to support the creation of practical, evidence-informed resources and learning experiences, including webinars, e-learning modules, online instructor-led certificate courses, Communities of Practice (CoPs), information guides, and blog posts. Additional responsibilities may include researching and curating resource lists tailored to provider needs, contributing ideas for new training and resource development, helping expand access to tools that support resettlement service providers in their work, and supporting the development of cultural orientation and client-facing resources through Settle In, a digital platform which empowers newcomers to navigate life in the U.S. with confidence by providing timely, accurate, and culturally relevant information in multiple languages..

COMMITMENT: 8-10 months, start date flexible, 5-15 hours per week

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Support the development of new training and technical assistance resources (i.e. webinars, e-learning, Instructor-led certificate courses, Communities of Practice (CoPs), information guides, blog posts, etc.).
  • Create customized resource lists in response to requests for technical assistance
  • Where relevant, support project administration by assisting with course enrollment and student records tracking, communications with learners, virtual learning space monitoring and facilitation, template creation, etc.

LEARNING OBJECTIVES:

  • The intern will gain professional experience in the provision of training and technical assistance, including instructional design and resource development.
  • The intern will deepen their understanding of client-centered practices across the U.S. refugee resettlement system, including areas such as mental health and psychosocial support, education, healthcare access, employment, social support services, and family well-being.
  • The intern will gain experience with methods and technology used to disseminate learning.

REQUIREMENTS:

  • Currently enrolled in a master’s program in psychology, counseling, social work or a related field.
  • Very strong organizational and written communication skills, including the ability to effectively distill and present complex information in a concise, accessible way.
  • Digital literacy including working knowledge of MS Office (Word, PowerPoint, Teams, Excel) and Zoom (this internship is fully remote, so trainee should be comfortable communicating via email, chat and video conference)
  • Strong interpersonal skills, professional flexibility, and the ability to work in a high-paced environment with a diverse team on many different projects. Turning on video is expected in all live calls and prompt responses to emails and other communication are expected within working hours.
  • Experience working with refugee populations, in case management or therapeutic settings, or lived experience as a refugee or migrant are preferred but not required.

This position is an unpaid, fully remote internship. The organization does not provide financial compensation, including compensation for relocation assistance or reimbursement for other expenses.

Interested applicants should email a resume, and cover letter to and with the subject line Switchboard Training Intern.

Professional Standards: All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

Elite is the trusted automation platform for law firm operations across most of the world’s largest and most successful law firms. Elite has guided firms through every technology shift and today delivers the only cloud-native SaaS platform that unifies financial, invoice, time, and data management into a single system of action. With embedded AI, predictive analytics, and integrated payments, Elite’s products enable firms to shorten billing cycles, reduce write-offs, and unlock firm-wide insights, making financial operations the foundation for law firm innovation and growth. Learn more at elite.com.

Position Overview

Elite is hiring a Director , Platform & Intelligence Value Stream to own the value stream end to end — the shared platform foundation every Elite product is built on, together with the productization of our AI and data capabilities. You will own the roadmap for orchestration, conversational AI, rules, unified access, and the event backbone, and turn those services into a reusable foundation that our financial, work-to-cash, and internal business product lines build on rather than around.

This is both a strategy role and a delivery role. You will carry the what and why for the stream — a single prioritized backlog, roadmap sequencing, and requirements translation through release commitment and delivery — pair daily with an engineering delivery unit, and lead a small standing team of domain and analyst talent. Because the platform is horizontal, you will sit upstream of every customer-facing product line, and you will be measured on the return the stream delivers rather than on output volume.

Work Arrangement:​Remote​

Responsibilities

Own the Platform & Framework Foundation

  • Own the product roadmap for Elite's shared platform services — including workflow orchestration, conversational AI, and business rules — and sequence their maturity from foundation to scale.
  • Own the product direction for unified access and entitlements — authorization, user management, data-level security, and subscription-driven feature access across Elite applications.
  • Treat the platform as a product with internal customers, defining the patterns, contracts, and adoption paths by which other product teams consume shared services, so capability is built once and reused.
  • Partner with Engineering on the shared infrastructure and sequencing that let product teams build on the platform rather than around it.

Productize AI & Data

  • Own productization of workflow- and agent-driven capabilities that move customers beyond traditional reporting toward AI that takes action inside their day-to-day financial and legal workflows.
  • Turn data assets into productized offerings on a modern cloud data platform, with clear value metrics and pricing.
  • Shape product and go-to-market strategy for integrations that give customers richer, real-time access to their data, including through third-party AI tools.

Lead the Value Stream

  • Define and prioritize a single backlog around customer outcomes and return on investment, and drive it from backlog through release commitment and delivery.
  • Set quarterly outcomes for the stream and point the paired delivery unit at the highest-value work; own feasibility, trade-offs, escalations, and backlog readiness.
  • Lead and grow the stream's standing team of domain and analyst talent, raising the bar on domain depth and AI fluency.
  • Act as the product voice in architectural and platform prioritization, steering infrastructure investment toward the capabilities that drive customer outcomes and revenue.

Build Governance In from the Start

  • Partner with Security and Architecture from the outset of each initiative to build data governance, access control, auditability, and appropriate safeguards into agentic products and integrations that handle privileged and financial data.
  • Ensure agents inherit user-level permissions, including data-level security, so intelligence and automation stay within firm entitlements by design.

Commercialize and Enable

  • Define value metrics and commercial models that make return on investment legible to customers and to the business.
  • Enable Sales and Services with clear narratives, value propositions, and routing guidance for platform, AI, and data capabilities.
  • Use usage data, customer insight, and financial metrics to drive prioritization for adoption, retention, and revenue impact.
  • Perform other duties as assigned to support departmental and company objectives.​

Qualifications

  • ​​Bachelor's Degree​ or equivalent education and experience.
  • 10+ years in product management, including direct ownership of platform, data, analytics, or AI/ML products, with at least three years leading product managers or end-to-end delivery.
  • Demonstrated experience productizing AI/ML or agentic capabilities into shipped B2B products — not only analytics or BI reporting. This is a core requirement.
  • Hands-on experience productizing platform or foundational services — workflow and orchestration, identity and entitlements, rules engines, or shared data services — consumed by multiple product teams.
  • Experience building or productizing data offerings on a modern cloud data platform or lakehouse architecture (for example Microsoft Fabric, Databricks, or Snowflake), with the technical fluency to make sound build trade-offs.
  • Experience packaging, pricing, and commercializing data products or platform integrations, including connectors or APIs that expose data to third-party tools or AI assistants.
  • Direct experience with data governance, access control, or compliance in a regulated or sensitive-data setting, and comfort partnering closely with Security and Architecture.
  • A track record of end-to-end delivery ownership — turning strategy into measurable, shipped outcomes — with fluency in backlog management and outcome metrics.
  • Proven people leadership: hiring, developing, and directing product and analyst talent, and leading through influence across Engineering and business partners.

jobs.description:
Twoja praca będzie głównie związana z:

  • developmentem w technologiach PHP7, Laravel, MySQL
  • frontendem w oparciu o JS-owy framework Vue.js/React/Angular
