jobs.excerpt: What We’re BuildingHoneycomb is a service for the near and present future, defining observability and raising expectations of what developer tools can do!
jobs.description:
What We’re Building

Honeycomb is a service for the near and present future, defining observability and raising expectations of what developer tools can do! We’re working with well known companies like HelloFresh, Slack, LaunchDarkly, and Vanguard and more across a range of industries. This is an exciting time in our trajectory, we’ve closed Series D funding, scaled past the 200-person mark, and were named to Forbes’ America’s Best Startups of 2022 and 2023!
If you want to see what we’ve been up to, please check out these blog posts and Honeycomb.io press releases.

Who We Are

We come for the impact, and stay for the culture! We’re a talented, opinionated, passionate, fiercely inclusive, and responsible group of bees. We have conviction and we strive to live our values every day. We want our people to do what they truly love amongst a team of highly talented (but humble) peers.

How We Work

We are a fully distributed company, which means we believe it is not where you sit, but how you deliver that matters most. We invest in our people and care about how you orient to our culture and processes. At the same time we imbue a lot of trust, autonomy, and accountability from Day 1.

Little more about the team:

AI agents at Honeycomb investigate, reason, and act on real observability data. They live in Canvas: the agentic workspace where engineers go to understand their systems.

The Agentic Intelligence team has shipped Canvas, the Honeycomb MCP server, and the Canvas Agent and Canvas Skills surfaces. What we're looking for today is someone who brings deep agent expertise and uses it to expand what the team can build: new agents, new surface area in Canvas, memory, spatial awareness, improved performance on our Bedrock loop.

Honeycomb's data store is fast and accepts high cardinality data; that's what makes agents built on top of it different from anything built on a conventional observability backend. This role is about taking advantage of that building agents that can do things no other observability product can do because the underlying data makes it possible.

Some of this work will start as a prototype. The expectation is that the code makes it through the full arc, from the rough first version through to something that holds up in production.

What you'll do

  • Design and deliver production-grade agents. Build agents that investigate, reason, and act on live observability data inside Canvas. These agents must be trustworthy to engineers in high pressure situations, including mid-incident. Take one from rough first version to something that holds up under production traffic.
  • Own the agent work; support the whole product. Scope, build, ship, and maintain the agents including the evals that tell you whether they got better or are just different. This role is agent-focused and also includes some fullstack development.
  • Build agents only Honeycomb can build. Use a data store that returns high-cardinality queries in seconds to reason over signal a conventional backend can't serve at this fidelity correlating across services, drilling into a single trace, comparing before and after a deploy.
  • Extend the surface, and decide what's next. Ship new capability into Canvas, the MCP server, and Canvas Skills memory, spatial awareness, a faster Bedrock loop and make the case for what comes after with working code. Distinguish hype from signal in a field with plenty of both.
  • Define what "good" means for agents here. Set the bar: measurable against real evals, maintainable, and honest about their limits.

Example projects

  • Multiple agents collaborating on one shared Canvas investigation each claiming a hypothesis, publishing findings, and narrowing the search space for the others so it resolves faster (blog).
  • Auto-investigation the moment an SLO burn alert fires the agent forms hypotheses and prepares visualizations before a human looks, cutting mean-time-to-insight for on-call (o11ycon 2026).
  • Skills that encode a team's domain expertise e.g. Kubernetes thresholds so agents and human colleagues can lean on them (o11ycon 2026).

What you'll bring:

  • AI and agent engineering experience. You've shipped LLM-based systems people relied on in production not demos, not fine-tuned models in a research context. You know where agent systems break and how to design around it.
  • End-to-end ownership. On a small team there's no handoff queue. You can take something from rough prototype to production-grade without needing someone behind you to do the durable engineering.
  • Current judgment, not just past experience. You have informed opinions about what's shifted in agent design in the last six to twelve months that would change how you'd build today.
  • Agent architecture depth. You understand how a fast, high-cardinality data store changes what an agent can reason about, and how to design for that.
  • Product judgment. You can look at what the agent layer does today and see what it should do next and make that case with a prototype, not a deck.

Even better

  • Observability or developer-tools background. Engineers are your users; you'll ramp faster with fluency in that world, and the work is better.
  • Familiarity with eval frameworks, agent tooling, RAG, and prompt engineering.
Base Salary based on level of experience
$183,340—$206,000 USD

What you'll get when you join the Hive:

  • A stake in our success - generous equity with employee-friendly stock program
  • It’s not about how strong of a negotiator you are - our pay is based on transparent levels relative to experience
  • Time to recharge with unlimited PTO
  • A distributed-first mindset and culture (really!)
  • Home office, co-working, and internet stipend
  • Full benefits coverage for employees, with additional coverage available for dependents
  • Up to 16 weeks of paid parental leave, regardless of path to parenthood
  • Annual development allowance
  • And much more...
Please note we cannot currently sponsor or support visa transfers at this time. Additionally, in compliance with applicable law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work.

Phishing and Recruitment Scam Warning:

We take your security seriously. Please be aware that recruitment scams are increasingly common and scammers may create email addresses or websites to impersonate Honeycomb employees. To help protect you:
  • All communications will come from an @honeycomb.io email address
    • We occasionally work with external recruiting agencies. These partners will use legitimate business email addresses—never personal accounts like Gmail or Yahoo.
  • Our recruiting process will never ask you to provide financial or sensitive personal information, including but not limited to:
    • Social security or tax identification numbers
    • Credit card numbers
    • Bank account information

Diversity & Accommodations:

We're committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and equitable workplace—where people of all backgrounds, identities, experiences, and abilities are welcomed, valued, and supported. We recognize that there is no single path to success and embrace nontraditional career journeys and diverse perspectives as key to building stronger, more innovative teams.
We strive to ensure an inclusive experience throughout every stage of our hiring process and are happy to provide reasonable accommodations as needed. If you require accommodations or accessible formats at any point during our hiring process, please let your recruiter know.
As an equal opportunity employer our hiring process is designed to put you at ease and help you show your best work. If there’s anything we can do to improve your experience, we’re always open to feedback.

We retain this information for various reasons, including in case we face a legal challenge in respect of a recruitment decision, to consider you for other current or future jobs at Honeycomb, and to help us better understand, analyze and improve our recruitment processes.

About CoLab

At CoLab, we help mechanical engineering teams bring life-changing products to market years sooner.

CoLab is the AI platform for driving stronger engineering decisions. Every design review in CoLab builds a knowledge repository of design feedback, decisions, and lessons learned - which AI agents draw from to flag issues on future designs before they compound. The more your team works in CoLab, the smarter it gets and the faster you arrive at the ideal design. Companies like Ford, Komatsu, and Johnson Controls use CoLab to catch issues earlier, eliminate rework cycles, and bring products to market faster.

Founded in St. John’s, Newfoundland, CoLab has grown quickly from our first customer in 2019 to a rapidly scaling company. We’ve recently been recognized on Deloitte’s Fast 50™ and Fast 500™, and named a Canadian company to watch by The Globe and Mail and Financial Post.

Role Summary

This role is a high-leverage operator reporting into the Director of Industry Strategy & Transformation, with direct exposure to revenue leadership and account owners. This role exists to define how CoLab wins with systems engineering organizations, connecting design review decisions to the requirements, interfaces, and verification work systems engineers own, and positioning CoLab as part of how complex products get engineered end to end.

Complex products fail at the boundaries. Requirements drift as designs mature, interfaces between mechanical, electrical, and software teams get negotiated in hallway conversations, and integration and test surface issues that a design review should have caught months earlier. Systems engineering exists to manage that complexity. You will define how CoLab plugs into it, earn the trust of chief engineers and digital engineering leaders, and turn that alignment into a repeatable path for expansion across programs and disciplines.

This is a deal-facing, customer-facing, and product-influencing role. The right person is part strategist, part operator, part competitor. Someone who can read a room of executives, build a hyper compelling value case on the fly, talk requirements traceability with a chief engineer and program risk with a CFO in the same afternoon, and close out the next step before the meeting ends.

Responsibilities

  • Define and own CoLab’s systems engineering strategy, including how design review decisions connect to requirements, interface management, and verification, and how CoLab fits alongside MBSE and requirements tools like Cameo, DOORS, and Jama.
  • Run workshops with chief engineers, systems engineering managers, and design teams that map who owns requirements and interfaces, where cross-discipline reviews break down, and where issues escape into integration and test, creating the urgency needed to mobilize multi-stakeholder buying groups.
  • Build the value case for systems and digital engineering leaders, grounded in requirements traceability, interface issues caught earlier, fewer late-stage design changes, and reduced integration and test risk.
  • Co-own deal strategy on strategic opportunities where systems engineering sits in the buying group, partnering with account executives to coach champions, orchestrate alignment across engineering disciplines, program leadership, and IT, and build the executive narratives that move buying groups forward.
  • Package systems engineering plays that account executives and customer engineers can run without you in the room, from discovery angles by SE maturity to expansion from one program to cross-program adoption.
  • Synthesize and share signals from strategic accounts into structured product feedback on requirements, MBSE integrations, and cross-discipline collaboration, validate product concepts with key customers, and support the Director of Industry Strategy & Transformation with market trends, competitive dynamics, and where digital engineering and MBSE adoption are heading.

Who You Are

  • A mechanical engineer by background, with real-world experience in product development, engineering processes, and design collaboration.
  • You’ve practiced systems engineering at a high level and have a deep understanding of the function. You bring direct experience as a systems engineer, chief engineer, or systems or digital engineering leader in complex product development, ideally in automotive, aerospace, defense, industrial equipment, or medical devices. You know requirements decomposition, interface control, trade studies, and V&V from the inside.
  • You think in systems. You see how choices in one discipline ripple into others, and you can spot where a program’s real risk lives before anyone else in the room.
  • High emotional intelligence and the ability to read a room of executives in real time. You know when to push, when to pause, when to ask the harder question, and when to take the win and move on.
  • Competitive by nature. You are wired to play to win, you put in the reps, and you run at high cadence. You take losses personally enough to learn from them and not personally enough to slow down.
  • Strong context switching ability. You can move from a board level value conversation to a requirements walkthrough to a workflow mapping session back to back and bring the right focus to each one.
  • Sharp sense of time value. You understand which work compounds, which work is throwaway, and which conversations are worth a calendar hold versus a quick Slack. You make calls and you move.
  • Strong commercial acumen and the ability to translate technical capability into business outcomes that resonate with VPs of Engineering, chief engineers, CEOs, and CFOs.
  • Operationally wired. You understand how work actually gets done inside complex organizations. You can spot process drag and connect workflow-level friction to business-level cost. You don’t just diagnose, you translate it into a path forward.
  • Clear, direct communicator. You write concisely, present without filler, and can build a clean, compelling deck under pressure. You know that a strong deck is a forcing function, not a deliverable, and you build them that way.
  • Fluent with AI tools as a force multiplier. You know how to use AI to compress research, sharpen messaging, and build faster. You don’t just tolerate the tools, you intentionally reach for them to do more with less.

What Success Looks Like in Year One

  • You have defined CoLab’s systems engineering strategy, and systems and digital engineering leaders at multiple strategic accounts are sponsoring CoLab as a result.
  • You are owning systems engineering workshops with our top enterprise accounts.
  • Your systems engineering plays are in use across the revenue team, with cross-program expansion you can point to.
  • You have meaningfully influenced the outcome of multiple seven figure deals.
  • You are trusted to drive customer conversations without backup.

jobs.description:
We're Hiring

Remote Academic Coach & Student Assistant (Part-Time, ~10 hours/week)

The steady partner who helps a high-achieving student master hard material and never miss a deadline.

About the Role

Seamless Assist is hiring a part-time Academic Coach & Student Assistant for a US-based family. You will work one-on-one, online, with their daughter, a motivated high-school student taking classes a year ahead of her grade, including several college-level Advanced Placement (AP) courses. This role reports to the student's parent.

Why This Role Exists

The student doesn't need to be taught from scratch. She is carrying a demanding, writing-heavy course load, and the pressure is in the volume: essays, problem sets, labs, tests and extracurricular deadlines all landing in the same week. This role exists to give her a sharp, organised partner who can keep up with advanced material, help her work through the hardest parts, and keep her schedule under control so nothing slips.

Her Current Classes

  • AP Microeconomics & Macroeconomics
  • AP Biology
  • AP English Language & Composition
  • AP US History
  • Pre-Calculus
  • Spanish 4
  • Journalism & News Production

You don't need to be an expert in every subject. You do need to be strong in several of them, especially writing-heavy courses (AP English Language, AP US History) and at least one of economics, biology or maths.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

Academic coaching (about 70% of your time)

  • Run live one-on-one video sessions to work through homework, problem sets, essays and test preparation.
  • Explain difficult concepts clearly and check that she can explain them back.
  • Review essays and written work for argument, structure, evidence and citations, including AP-style timed essays.
  • Build practice questions, review plans and study guides ahead of tests and the AP exams in May.
  • Learn how each course is taught and graded (syllabi, teacher rubrics, the College Board AP course frameworks) and coach to them.
  • Coach, never complete. Her work must always be her own, in line with her school's academic integrity rules.

Planning and student assistant support (about 30% of your time)

  • Run a weekly planning session: map every class's assignments, tests and deadlines into a shared calendar and task list.
  • Keep her schedule current across classes, activities and appointments, with study time blocked in.
  • Send short reminders before deadlines and confirm work was actually submitted.
  • Track grades and flag early when something starts to slip.
  • Send the parent a short weekly progress update.

Schedule

About 10 hours per week. Sessions fall on weekday afternoons and evenings, US Pacific Time (roughly 3:30–8:30 pm PT), plus one short weekend planning session. You must be reliably available in that window.

Who Will Succeed in This Role

This is a high-trust role with a bright, busy teenager. You will need real subject depth, patience, and the organisational discipline of a strong executive assistant.

  • You explain things clearly and can tell the difference between "I get it" and actually getting it.
  • You are a strong writer and can give specific, useful feedback on an argumentative essay.
  • You run your own life from a calendar and a task list, and you follow up without being asked.
  • You are warm, steady and encouraging, and you hold a high standard.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree or higher, ideally in education, English, history, economics, biology, mathematics or a related field.
  • At least 2 years of tutoring or teaching high-school or first-year university students.
  • Strong command of the material in several of the subjects listed above.
  • Excellent written and spoken English. Your writing will be assessed during screening.
  • Uses AI tools in your daily work (for example Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini) to build study materials and plan faster, and can teach a student to use them responsibly and within school rules.
  • Able to work US Pacific Time afternoons and evenings, about 10 hours per week.
  • Reliable high-speed internet, a quiet workspace, a webcam and a backup power or internet plan.
  • Willing to complete a national police clearance or background check and provide two professional references before starting.

Nice to have

  • Experience with the US Advanced Placement (AP) programme, or strong AP, SAT, IB or A-Level results of your own.
  • Conversational or better Spanish.
  • Journalism, editing or newsroom experience.
  • Comfortable in Google Workspace (Calendar, Docs, Drive) and a task tool such as Notion or Todoist.

How We Work

Because this role involves working one-on-one with a teenager, clear safeguards apply. All sessions run on a family-owned video account and are recorded. All messages go through a group channel that includes a parent. There is no private messaging or social-media contact with the student. A background check and references are required before the first paid session.

Pay

Competitive hourly pay, paid monthly in USD. Pay varies by country.

How to Apply

Apply with your CV. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to a short AI-led video interview, a written subject task, an interview with the family and a paid trial session.

jobs.title: Order Resolution Program Manager
jobs.excerpt: Positition:The Order Resolution Program Manager builds and leads the Order Resolution Program (ORP), a national program that helps ensure patients receive the testing their physicians have ordered.
jobs.description:
Positition:

The Order Resolution Program Manager builds and leads the Order Resolution Program (ORP), a national program that helps ensure patients receive the testing their physicians have ordered. When an order encounters a barrier, such as an unreachable patient, an incorrect phone number, a patient with unanswered questions about their test, or a step that requires clinic involvement, this role makes sure the right people take the right action so care is not delayed. Many of these patients are navigating a cancer diagnosis, and the program exists to support them and the Patient Coordinators who care for them.

As the program's founding owner, the Program Manager exercises independent judgment to assess the current landscape, resolve complex cases directly, and determine what the program needs to succeed, including whether and how to expand the team. The role is hands-on by design: the Program Manager works open cases alongside Patient Coordinators to understand where and why orders stall, then uses that firsthand insight and program data to set strategy, define standards, and guide leadership decisions.

The Program Manager partners across Patient Services, Territory Managers, Clinical Oncology Specialists, Patient Coordinators, Inside Sales Managers, Regional Directors, and Operations Managers, earning alignment through expertise and sound judgment rather than direct authority.

Primary Responsibilities:

Program Strategy & Ownership

  • Own the Order Resolution Program end-to-end across all national regions, independently assessing the current landscape, including case volume, root causes, regional variation, and existing workflows, to determine where patient orders are most at risk of delay.
  • Develop a data-supported program roadmap and staffing recommendation for Patient Services leadership, including headcount requirements, staffing structure, timeline, and whether process or tooling solutions would better serve patients.
  • Define the program operating model, including case ownership, escalation criteria, service timelines, handoff protocols, and quality standards, and adjust it as the program matures.
  • Lead the design of the team structure, role definitions, hiring profile, onboarding, and performance expectations for future team members.

Case Resolution & Patient Care Support

  • Exercise independent judgment to evaluate open ORP cases, determine the root cause of each barrier, and develop a tailored resolution strategy that accounts for the clinical context, the patient's circumstances, and available resources.
  • Work complex and high-priority cases directly, including researching LIMS, paper orders, and patient outreach tools to locate missing or updated contact information, and decide whether a case calls for administrative resolution, clinic education or engagement, or escalation.
  • Partner with Patient Coordinators to support patient outreach, providing guidance on how to approach each case and, where appropriate, connecting with patients directly so that questions about their orders are answered and care can move forward.
  • Determine when to escalate a case to the clinic, engage the field team, or close it, and document the rationale so any subsequent owner can continue seamlessly.
  • Maintain a real-time view of all open cases, including status, owner, next action, and age, and follow up consistently to confirm actions are completed and patients are not left waiting.

Analytics & Performance Reporting

  • Design, build, and maintain the ORP reporting infrastructure, including dashboards, KPI scorecards, and regional trend analysis, and define the metrics used to measure program success.
  • Report regularly to Patient Services leadership on case volume, resolution rates, time to resolution, and order completion outcomes, translating data into clear insights about what is working, what is not, and what should change.
  • Analyze recurring barriers, such as common reasons patients cannot be reached or questions that arise repeatedly, and develop recommendations that reduce the number of patients whose orders require intervention in the first place.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Process Improvement

  • Partner with Territory Managers, Clinical Oncology Specialists, Associate Clinical Oncology Specialists, and Patient Coordinators to set clear expectations, communicate promptly, and share accountability on every open case.
  • Partner with Inside Sales Managers, Regional Directors, and Operations Managers to align program priorities, resolve regional barriers, and ensure teams understand their role in supporting patient orders.
  • Serve as the subject matter expert for ORP, providing guidance and consultation to field and operations partners and developing best practices, training, and standard work that can be adopted nationally.
  • Identify systemic process gaps and bring structured, data-backed recommendations to leadership, including changes to workflows, status definitions, tooling, and cross-team handoffs, with the patient experience as the guiding lens.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in healthcare administration, business, life sciences, or a related field; or equivalent professional experience in a role requiring independent judgment, program ownership, and decision-making in a healthcare or clinical operations environment.
  • 5 or more years of experience in healthcare operations, patient services, program or project management, or a comparable environment, with demonstrated ownership of a program, workflow, or initiative from assessment through execution.
  • Demonstrated ability to assess a complex operating landscape, identify root causes, and develop and present a data-supported recommendation, including resourcing and staffing needs, to senior leadership.
  • Proven ability to independently assess multi-variable situations and determine the appropriate course of action without direct supervision, particularly in patient-facing or clinically sensitive contexts.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence and drive accountability across cross-functional teams, including field, sales, and operations leaders, without direct authority.
  • Strong analytical capability, including building performance reporting, interpreting trends, and communicating findings clearly to leadership; advanced MS Excel or equivalent skills required.
  • Experience in a call center, patient outreach, or high-volume case management environment (inbound and outbound).
  • Proficiency in CRM platforms, case tracking systems, and data tools; familiarity with skip tracing tools and LIMS is a strong plus.
  • Prior experience leading, coaching, or building a team is preferred. Background in patient coordination or another patient-facing healthcare role is strongly preferred.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Technical

  • Program and project management expertise, including scoping, planning, prioritization, milestone tracking, and stakeholder management.
  • Specialized knowledge of healthcare operations, patient services workflows, and clinical coordination sufficient to evaluate case scenarios and develop resolution strategies without relying on standardized scripts.
  • Advanced proficiency in CRM platforms, case tracking systems, and reporting tools, with the ability to design KPI dashboards that give leadership real-time visibility into program performance and patient order outcomes.
  • Strong quantitative skills, including comfort working with large data sets to identify trends, build business cases, and model staffing and capacity needs.
  • Experience with skip tracing tools and multi-database research methods, and with process documentation and standard operating procedure development.

Behavioral

  • Exercises sound, independent judgment consistently, treating each case and each program decision as a situation requiring individualized analysis.
  • Builds before being asked: sees what a new program needs, takes ownership of the decision, and moves forward without waiting to be told something is off track.
  • Balances urgency and care: moves quickly because patients are waiting, and makes thoughtful decisions because the stakes are real.
  • Thinks like a program owner and acts like a teammate: comfortable working individual cases to learn the work, and equally comfortable stepping back to set strategy and advise leadership.
  • Earns credibility with cross-functional partners through expertise, clear communication, and follow-through, and uses it to drive action across teams they do not directly control.
  • Coaches and develops others, and is ready to build and lead a team as the program grows.

Physical Demands & Work Environment:

  • This is a primarily remote position. Occasional on-site attendance may be required for planning sessions, leadership reviews, or business needs.
  • Duties are performed in a home office or professional office setting and require the ability to use a computer keyboard, communicate over the telephone, and read printed and digital material.
  • This role may require working outside standard business hours at times to address time-sensitive case situations or program needs.

Travel:

Minimal travel required. Occasional travel (estimated less than 15%) may be required for national leadership meetings, regional business reviews, or planning sessions.

Job Posting Closing Date: Open until Filled

Where do you belong?

Your career is more than just a job, it's part of your life. Whether you’re a clinician, or non-clinical professional, at USACS you'll feel a sense of connection working with clinicians and office staff who share your interests and values. We want you to love coming to work each day because you believe in what you do and the people with whom you work. We care about your success.

USACS also understands that location is important. We offer career opportunities for clinicians and non-clinical support staff from New York to Hawaii and numerous points in between. Our supportive culture, outstanding benefits and competitive compensation package is best in class.

Job Description

The Clinician Documentation Educator is responsible for analyzing ERP trend sheet, PCCI and open coder comms reports for deficiency trends. Proactively notify clinicians of their deficiencies per escalation SOP.

Location: Remote


ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:

  • Analyzes coder communication and other reports for trends.
  • Reviews medical records and identifies potential gaps in clinical documentation for emergency medicine and payer populations (e.g., Medicare, Medicaid, Blue Cross/Blue Shield, etc.) as directed.
  • Identify and trend erroneous coder communication.
  • Remains current in EHR/EMR capabilities and updates. Works with site Directors and EHR/EMR reps to ensure proper documentation, compliance with CMS, CPT, ICD-10 and USACS guidelines and ensure that USACS receives a chart extract containing all necessary components.
  • Analyzes reports for trends. Data is reviewed and manipulated to provide clinician feedback for documentation improvement.
  • Maintains knowledge of current trends, practices and principles of documentation and government regulations through reading materials and/or attending educational seminars.
  • Performs and assists with coding and other department duties as needed.
  • Demonstrates basic knowledge of coding standards and application to ongoing evaluation of medical record documentation
  • Consistently meets established productivity targets for record review

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

  • Knowledge of and experience using ICD-9-CM, ICD-10-CM and CPT and HCPCS coding.
  • Knowledge of payer guidelines.
  • Knowledge of and skill using personal computers in a Windows environment with an emphasis on word processing, spreadsheets, and data entry.
  • Ability to pay close attention to detail.
  • Ability to identify, research and solve problems and discrepancies.
  • Ability to organize data and produce outcome statistics.
  • Ability to professionally and effectively communicate in writing or verbally with physicians, coworkers, management, and third-party payers.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality.
  • Ability to effectively perform in a multi-task work environment.
  • Ability to process assigned duties in an organized manner.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • RHIT, RHIA, CPC, CCS-P, or other job-related accreditation required.
  • At least one year of coding experience or equivalent training/education.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of industry guidelines and regulations required.

Hourly Rate: $22.84-$43.27

Hourly rate may be determined on several factors including but not limited to knowledge, skills, experience, education, geographical location and requirements stated in job description.

  • 401(k) employee and employer contributions

  • Paid parental leave & family support benefits

jobs.excerpt: As a team member in Finance at Nationwide, a Fortune 100 company with nearly $70 billion in annual sales, the opportunities are endless!
jobs.description:
As a team member in Finance at Nationwide, a Fortune 100 company with nearly $70 billion in annual sales, the opportunities are endless! Let Nationwide help create your career journey! At Nationwide®, “on your side” goes beyond just words. Our customers are at the center of everything we do and we’re looking for associates who are passionate about delivering extraordinary care.

Nationwide’s Commercial Lines team is hiring a Predictive Modeler / Pricing Modeler to help shape sophisticated insurance pricing models and deliver insights that influence business decisions. This role is ideal for someone who brings strong technical modeling skills and either a solid actuarial foundation, commercial insurance knowledge, or both.


In this position, you will work at the intersection of predictive analytics, actuarial thinking, and pricing strategy. You will partner closely with teammates and business partners to build, enhance, and refine models that support commercial insurance pricing. You will also have the opportunity to work across a variety of projects, expand your technical toolkit, and deepen your understanding of how modeling drives real business outcomes.


What makes this opportunity stand out:


  • A unique blend of predictive modeling, pricing, and commercial actuarial work
  • Highly visible projects that support important pricing decisions
  • The chance to work with R, Python, SQL, and modern modeling techniques in a business-critical environment
  • Exposure to insurance data, actuarial mechanics, and the nuances of commercial lines pricing
  • A collaborative team structure where modeling, actuarial, and business expertise come together
  • Broad skill development across predictive analytics, actuarial concepts, and cross-functional partnership
  • The opportunity to contribute quickly if you already understand insurance, actuarial modeling, or pricing workflows

We are especially interested in candidates who can combine technical modeling ability with practical business application. Strong candidates may come from actuarial, predictive modeling, pricing analytics, or data science backgrounds, but they should be excited by insurance use cases and motivated to work in a role where actuarial and modeling foundations both matter.


The strongest profiles will typically offer a mix of the following:


  • Predictive modeling or pricing model experience
  • Commercial insurance, property and casualty, or broader insurance analytics experience
  • Knowledge of actuarial concepts, pricing mechanics, or loss cost / relativity-based thinking
  • Hands-on coding experience in R, Python, SQL, or similar analytical tools
  • The ability to translate data into actionable pricing or underwriting insight
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work through technical detail in a collaborative setting

This is not a pure data science role removed from the business, and it is not a traditional actuarial role in the narrow sense. It is a hybrid opportunity for someone who wants to apply predictive modeling in a commercial actuarial and insurance pricing environment, learn from strong partners, and grow into an even more versatile analytics professional.


If you want to build models that matter, strengthen your pricing and actuarial expertise, and work on meaningful commercial insurance challenges, this role offers the chance to do exactly that. This role can be staffed remote.

Job Description Summary

Do you have the desire to analyze data and perform groundbreaking research to drive business outcomes? Nationwide has been using data to serve our members and drive business outcomes for almost 100 years. Our industry-leading workforce adopts an agile work environment and a collaborative culture to deliver outstanding solutions and results. Our Risk Analytics Researchers play a key role in harnessing the power of data to deliver business results. Specifically, they are responsible for modeling sophisticated problems, discovering insights and identifying business opportunities from data using a variety of techniques from mathematics, actuarial studies, statistics, data science and financial engineering.

As a Consultant, you’ll work on projects associated with the design, development, and application of unique risk models. You’ll need a basic understanding of broad business objectives and will work with business partners across the finance organization to develop solutions to pressing business needs. We’ll count on you to be a subject matter authority in Nationwide’s risks. It’s imperative that you are fully proficient with basic and sophisticated mathematical, statistical and analytical techniques associated with risk modeling.

Job Description

Key Responsibilities:

  • Researches and implements financial engineering, data science and statistical techniques for risk management and business applications.

  • Completes regular testing of risk limits to provide distinct management guidance on asset allocation, risk transfer and product growth decisions.

  • Owns complex quantitative modeling processes and philosophies. Identifies industry standards to understand if models are working as intended.

  • Collaborates to ensure that consistent model assumptions, processes and outputs are well understood and that modeling standard methodologies are upheld.

  • Reviews and analyzes model output to identify model limitations and their impact. Provides corrective quantitative methods.

  • Crafts and updates model documentation for business continuity purposes.

  • Collaborates to develop creative solutions to business problems.

  • Acts as the technology owner for Risk Analytics.

May perform other responsibilities as assigned.

Reporting Relationships: Reports to Risk/Actuarial leader.

Typical Skills and Experiences:

Education: Undergraduate studies in finance, accounting, economics, statistics, mathematics or related subject area required. Graduate-level studies in a related field with advanced degree highly desirable.

License/Certification/Designation: Progress toward FCAS, FSA, CQF, CFA or similar preferred.

Experience: Typically, five or more years of related work experience in financial risk modeling or actuarial functions.

Knowledge, Abilities and Skills: Working knowledge of machine learning, stochastic processes, Monte Carlo simulations, sampling methods and other statistical techniques applicable to specialized risk modeling. Prefer mathematical knowledge of specialized risk models such as those used in hedging, economic scenario generation, catastrophe, credit risk, etc. Solid understanding of risk management operations such as asset-liability management, portfolio risk assessment, hedging, etc. Proficient written and verbal communication skills. Intermediate proficiency with Excel and common statistical software such as R, SAS, Python, or MATLAB.

Other criteria, including leadership skills, competencies and experiences may take precedence.

Staffing exceptions to the above must be approved by the hiring manager’s leader and Human Resources Business Partner.

Values: Regularly and consistently demonstrates Nationwide Values.

Job Conditions:

Overtime Eligibility: Not Eligible (Exempt)

Working Conditions: Normal office environment.

Job Title: Commissioning Coordinator

Location: UK (Remote)

The Commissioning Coordinator will be an integral part of the commissioning team, with their main responsibility being to work with and support the commissioning engineer and their manager in the commissioning of BESS sites. The successful candidate must be able and willing to travel and complete tasks at various project sites throughout the country and, on occasion, internationally. Experience with BESS or renewable power generation equipment in a commissioning or service environment is required.

Responsibilities:

  • Commission BESS sites using CSI Energy Storage’s Solbank Storage Power Block as part of a commissioning team.
  • Perform tasks assigned by the commissioning manager and engineer, such as safety system checks, installation inspections, and functional tests.
  • Perform daily routine tasks such as executing commissioning checklists, reviewing and updating the issues list, and helping to monitor the performance of commissioned assets.
  • Support the commissioning of the overall control system by testing the network connectivity of all field devices and performing point-to-point tests.
  • Provide on-site diagnostic, troubleshooting, and hands-on support.
  • Supervise subcontractors on-site where required.
  • Assist in developing standard operating procedures from lessons learned on-site.
  • Assist with the completion of testing documentation and preparation of test reports in a timely manner.
  • Assist with the identification and compilation of spare parts inventories.
  • Ensure proper LOTO and switching procedures are observed as required.
  • Support client and operation and maintenance contractor training during and after commissioning.
  • Adhere to all health and safety rules and policies.
  • Attend and occasionally lead Plan of Day (POD) meetings.
  • Review vendor commissioning documentation for completeness and accuracy.
  • Maintain deficiencies punch list for each vendor and track completion of various tasks.
  • Work with the commissioning engineer to ensure post-handover site performance is optimized.

Qualifications and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in project management, or a related field preferred (but not mandatory).
  • Equivalent professional experience in project coordination or management will be considered.
  • Minimum 5 years of experience in project management, commissioning coordination, or related roles within energy storage, renewable energy, or utility-scale projects.
  • Proven ability to manage multiple projects and priorities while adhering to deadlines.
  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate with cross-functional teams, delegate tasks, and foster collaboration.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills for engaging with internal teams, clients, and contractors.
  • Proficiency in managing project documentation, preparing test reports, and submitting commissioning deliverables.
  • Ensures timely and accurate tracking, organization, and submission of required documentation to stakeholders.
  • Familiarity with the commissioning processes of energy storage systems or a related industry
  • Adaptability and Problem-Solving Skills
  • Capacity to quickly adapt to project changes and resolve challenges proactively.
  • Comfortable working in dynamic environments with shifting priorities.
  • Willingness to travel regionally or nationally to support commissioning activities and team needs.
  • Flexibility to support project sites as required.

jobs.description:
Nous recherchons un(e) gestionnaire, services techniques pour notre client, PrevTech. Vous serez le gestionnaire de proximité d’une équipe entièrement en télétravail et veillerez au bon fonctionnement des opérations quotidiennes du centre de contact clients. Vous jouerez également un rôle clé dans la qualité de l’expérience offerte aux clients, en vous assurant que chaque intervention combine efficacité opérationnelle, jugement, empathie et prise en charge.

Nous cherchons avant tout une personne qui aime par-dessus tout gérer une équipe, coacher et faire grandir ses employés. Une personne humaine et accessible, avec une forte intelligence émotionnelle, mais aussi suffisamment structurée et orientée résultats pour responsabiliser son équipe et intervenir lorsque nécessaire.

Voici plus concrètement les différentes responsabilités qui vous attendent :

Gestion d’équipe, coaching et développement — 40 %

Être le point de référence d’une équipe de 8 représentants techniques au service à la clientèle et créer les conditions pour que chacun puisse bien performer et évoluer.

  • Créer une relation de confiance et maintenir une vraie proximité avec votre équipe, même à distance;

  • Tenir des rencontres individuelles régulières pour parler performance, défis, objectifs et développement;

  • Adapter votre gestion aux différentes personnalités, façons de travailler et niveaux d’autonomie de vos subalternes;

  • Coacher les employés pour développer leurs compétences, leur progression au sein de Prevtech et leurs réflexes de résolution de problèmes face aux différentes situations clients possibles;

  • Suivre la performance individuelle et collective à l’aide d’indicateurs clairs et contribuer à faire évoluer ces mécanismes de suivi;

  • Reconnaître les écarts de performance, de comportement ou d’assiduité et intervenir avec tact et fermeté;

  • Participer à l’intégration des nouveaux employés et contribuer à maintenir un climat positif et collaboratif.

Gestion quotidienne des opérations — 30 %

Vous assurez le bon déroulement des opérations au quotidien et veillez à ce que l'équipe soit bien alignée sur les priorités de service.

  • Collaborer étroitement avec la vice-présidente, une gestionnaire humaine, dynamique et axée sur les résultats, afin d’assurer la prise en charge des opérations quotidiennes du département et de lui permettre de se dégager davantage des opérations;

  • Suivre le volume d’alarmes, les cas ouverts et les suivis afin d’assurer une prise en charge rapide;

  • Veiller au respect des priorités et des délais de service;

  • Veiller à ce que les décisions opérationnelles et les interventions de l’équipe maintiennent une approche centrée sur le client, en recherchant le juste équilibre entre efficacité, qualité de service et prise en charge de la situation;

  • Planifier et ajuster les horaires selon les besoins, les absences et les imprévus;

  • Garder votre sang-froid et aider l’équipe à prioriser lorsque plusieurs situations surviennent en même temps;

  • Repérer les blocages et mettre rapidement en place des solutions concrètes;

  • Soutenir exceptionnellement les opérations lors d’une urgence ou d’une période plus intense.

Ce qui vous attend lors de votre intégration au poste :À votre arrivée, vous passerez du temps comme aviseur en surveillance technique afin de comprendre concrètement la réalité de votre équipe, les systèmes et les interventions. Une excellente façon de développer rapidement votre compréhension du terrain et votre crédibilité auprès de l’équipe.

Gestion des escalades — 15 %

Vous êtes le dernier niveau d’escalade managériale du centre de services techniques. Vous assurer que les situations plus complexes se rendent rapidement aux bonnes personnes et qu’aucun dossier ne tombe entre deux chaises. Vous intervenez directement lorsque la situation exige davantage de jugement, de coordination ou de gestion de la relation client.

  • Reconnaître rapidement une situation qui doit être escaladée;

  • Aider l’équipe à déterminer la prochaine étape lorsqu’un cas devient plus complexe ou ambigu;

  • Vous assurer que les cas sont transférés au bon niveau technique et en assurer le suivi;

  • Prendre directement en charge les escalades les plus sensibles ou complexes, notamment lorsqu’un client est insatisfait, qu’une situation se détériore ou qu’une intervention managériale est nécessaire;

  • Agir comme niveau ultime d’escalade lorsque les équipes techniques ou de première ligne ne sont pas en mesure de résoudre adéquatement la situation;

  • Prioriser lorsque plusieurs situations urgentes surviennent simultanément;

  • Coordonner les interventions avec les experts techniques, les autres équipes et les ressources externes lorsque nécessaire.

  • S’assurer qu’une escalade est menée jusqu’à une résolution claire, tant du point de vue opérationnel que de l’expérience client.

Qualité et amélioration continue — 15 %

Vous assurer que les standards de qualité de PrevTech sont maintenus par l’ensemble des membres de l’équipe et continuer à faire évoluer les façons de faire.

  • Évaluer la qualité des appels, textos, notes et suivis clients;

  • Donner une rétroaction concrète à la suite de l’écoute ou de l’analyse d’une intervention;

  • Animer des calibrations d’équipe pour maintenir des standards communs;

  • Repérer les écarts récurrents et déterminer si une procédure, une formation ou un outil doit être revu;

  • Faire évoluer les procédures, guides, outils et contenus de formation internes;

  • Proposer des solutions simples et applicables pour améliorer l’efficacité et la qualité du service.

Compétences recherchées

  • Encadrement;

  • Création d’équipes performantes;

  • Résolution de conflits;

  • Entrer en relation avec les autres;

  • Orientation vers les résultats;

  • Résolution de problèmes;

  • Gestion du stress;

  • Empathie.

Requis (expérience et qualification, langue)

  • Expérience minimale de 5 ans en gestion, supervision ou coordination d’une équipe de service à la clientèle, de soutien technique, d’opérations ou de première ligne;

  • Expérience concrète en coaching et en gestion de la performance d’une équipe;

  • Expérience dans un environnement où les priorités et le volume peuvent changer rapidement;

  • DEC pertinent ou combinaison équivalente de formation et d’expérience;

  • Bilinguisme français / anglais essentiel (plus de 50% des échanges avec les clients, collègues et partenaires sont en anglais);

  • Aisance avec les outils technologiques et capacité à apprendre rapidement de nouvelles plateformes.

Des atouts :

  • Expérience en gestion d’une équipe à distance;

  • Expérience dans un environnement technique ou technologique;

  • Formation en gestion, leadership ou ressources humaines.

Les défis qui vous attendent

  • Gérer une équipe, de jour et de soir, entièrement à distance demande une vraie capacité à créer de la proximité même sans être physiquement ensemble;

  • Maintenir une bonne qualité de service lorsque le volume augmente;

  • Contribuer à structurer les processus internes du département afin de soutenir la forte croissance de l’entreprise;

  • Parce que les alarmes ne suivent pas toujours un horaire de bureau, une certaine disponibilité en dehors des heures régulières sera nécessaire lors de situations urgentes.

Conditions de travail

  • Poste permanent à temps plein (40h/semaine);

  • 100 % télétravail, avec horaires flexibles;

  • 4 semaines de vacances dès l’entrée en poste;

  • 3 journées mobiles personnelles par année;

  • Cellulaire et ordinateur fournis;

  • Gamme d’avantages sociaux incluant :

    • Assurance collective après la période de probation;

    • Régime volontaire d’épargne-retraite (RVÉR) en développement;

  • Salaire annuel entre 68 000 $ et 94 000 $ selon expérience.

Écosystème technologique et système informatique utilisée

  • Plateforme propriétaire de gestion des cas clients;

  • Suite Google (communication et collaboration);

  • Salesforce (CRM et gestion de la relation client);

  • Autres outils technologiques à évaluer selon les recommandations du futur titulaire.

Un peu plus sur PrevTech et votre future équipe

PrevTech est une entreprise québécoise spécialisée en surveillance électrique intelligente et en prévention des incendies. Son centre de services techniques surveille à distance les alarmes provenant des systèmes installés chez ses clients. Lorsqu’une alarme est détectée, l’équipe intervient de façon proactive auprès du client, l’accompagne dans les premières vérifications et coordonne les prochaines étapes avec les ressources techniques appropriées. PrevTech connaît également une importante période de croissance : développement de ses activités aux États-Unis, évolution de sa plateforme interne et structuration continue de ses niveaux d’intervention technique.

jobs.description:
Role Title: Emerging Technology Threat / Strategic Competition Advisor

Role Type: Contractor (~15 hs/wk)

Location: Remote, US only

micro1 is engaging Emerging Technology Threat / Strategic Competition Advisors to contribute to a customer’s project focused on evaluating AI reasoning in strategic and threat assessment contexts. In this role, you’ll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.

Scope of Work

  1. Design and author realistic cases centered on emerging-technology threats—such as AI/autonomy, hypersonics, space, cyber, quantum, directed energy, and CBRN-adjacent domains—within the context of strategic competition dynamics.
  2. Apply net-assessment principles and strategic-competition analysis to ambiguous scenarios, assessing adversary intent, capability development, and the boundary between legitimate and prohibited analysis.
  3. Grade AI model outputs against criteria including analytical rigor, use of sources, handling of uncertainty, expression of limitations, and practical utility for strategy or targeting.
  4. Ensure scenario fidelity by validating that evaluation cases reflect authentic strategic and threat-assessment methodologies, not simplified or headline-driven versions.
  5. Identify and flag instances where the AI model unnecessarily refuses sound conceptual, analytic, or policy inquiries.
  6. Document edge cases and articulate the reasoning behind each assessment to ensure defensibility and transparency in evaluation.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Senior-level experience in strategic analysis, threat assessment, or net assessment at respected organizations—such as defense think tanks, intelligence community strategic shops, service futures/strategy offices, or combatant-command strategy/plans roles.

jobs.description:
Our Opportunity:

Building on Purdue University's mission to provide greater access to affordable, high-quality education, Purdue University Global is a public, nonprofit institution offering a world-class education online. Purdue Global delivers personalized online education tailored to the unique needs of adults who have work or life experience beyond the classroom, enabling them to develop essential academic and professional skills with the support and flexibility they need to achieve their career goals.

The Full-Time Faculty role will provide support to Purdue University Global’s College of Social and Behavioral Sciences.

Job Summary

Full-time faculty may have responsibilities in four areas: teaching, service, scholarship, and professional development. The amount of time spent in each area is determined on an annual basis, after discussion between the faculty member and their Department Chair, and may vary from year to year. The workload is based on the needs of the Department and School, consistent with the university’s mission as a teaching institution. While the majority of faculty typically spend the greatest percentage of their time teaching, there is the opportunity in a given year for the percentage of time in any category to change.

Teaching responsibilities may include both undergraduate and graduate courses. The number of courses assigned will consider credentials, program needs, course types, the number of different preparations, and the number of students served.

Service will typically include participating in and/or taking leadership roles in Purdue Global department or institution-wide governance committees. Service examples also include course lead, training and mentoring other faculty, facilitating student-focused organizations or activities, the evaluation of student portfolios, curriculum work, vacation relief for colleagues, and leadership in professional organizations. In limited cases, specific service activities may be assigned additional compensation. This role may require service as a Research Project Coordinator for Doctoral programs in the College of Social and Behavioral Sciences.

Scholarship activities vary with the interests of the individual faculty member and may not be required. Scholarship activities should be developed in consultation with the Dean, Associate Dean or Academic Chair. Examples of PG scholarship activities include developing and implementing solutions or new approaches to academic and professional challenges, as well as publishing articles related to research within the discipline or profession and/or presenting at academic or professional meetings.

Some professional development (8 hours) is required for all faculty over the course of a year. Faculty development beyond these minimum expectations may be considered part of an annual workload, if determined appropriate by the Academic Department Chair or requested by the faculty member and approved by the Department Chair.

A balance of these four responsibilities is intended to sustain the academic goals of the university to serve adult learners, and advance the professional goals of the faculty, while creating a supportive learning environment that provides students with a clear path to graduation.

Teaching is typically the primary assignment for a Purdue Global faculty member, with service, scholarship and additional professional development activities comprising the balance of the annual workload. If no assignments are made in service and scholarship, a faculty member whose only assignment is teaching would not exceed 16-18 courses taught in a year.

What to expect in this role:

  • Provides a student-centered learning environment which enables students to attain success.
  • Reports concerns regarding student academic progress to Success Coaches or Academic Advisors, as appropriate. Refers students with questions regarding financial aid, academics, attendance, and personal issues or concerns to the appropriate departments.
  • Actively assists the University in retention and/or outreach efforts, which may include directly contacting students who are not engaged in the course or absent per department or campus guidelines.
  • Maintains open and timely communication with students and the university via Purdue Global email. Reports student behavioral and Code of Student Conduct issues.
  • Participates in institutional assessment and assists Chairs and Deans to develop and implement new programs as assigned.
  • Regularly attends and participates in faculty meetings and continuous improvement sessions. Serves on university committees as assigned.
  • Remains current with trends, techniques, and advances in technology that are applicable to the program. Incorporates creative instructional strategies and/or learning activities.
  • Maintains and submits accurate and timely reports for student grades.
  • Follows university style and branding guidelines for materials that are created for students. Providing students with materials that always meet accessibility standards.
  • Serve as a Research Project Coordinator (RPC) for Doctoral programs in the College of Social and Behavioral Sciences.

Experience:

  • Doctoral degree in a Public Service, such as Criminal Justice, Fire Science, Criminology, or Emergency Management or closely related field. ABD not accepted.
  • Practitioner experience in Public Service, such as Criminal Justice, Fire Science, or Emergency Management or closely related fields is required.
  • Experience as a doctoral committee member or research faculty is preferred.
  • Minimum 2– 4 years related subject-matter work experience (online teaching experience a plus).

What we're looking for:

  • Exceptional computer skills using Microsoft Office Suite, Google applications and Zoom meeting technology. Experience with Brightspace education software is preferred.
  • Excellent communication, organizational and time management skills, and with the ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Ability to work effectively in a remote environment with minimal supervision.
  • Capable of building strong working relationships across teams, departments and Schools.
  • Ability to handle sensitive and confidential information with discretion.

Additional Information:

  • The target salary for this position is $65,000. Learn more about our Benefits Here!
  • Purdue University Global will not sponsor employment authorization for this position.
  • This is a U.S.-based position. This position is open to candidates who reside and are authorized to work in the United States.
  • A background check will be required for employment in this position.
  • We ask that our remote employees have access to a reliable internet connection and a dedicated, properly equipped workspace that is free of distractions. You may wish to review the Purdue Virtual Meeting Professional Standards.
  • When applying for a faculty position at Purdue University Global you will be asked to provide an unofficial transcript and if hired will be required to provide an official transcript.
  • FLSA: Exempt (Not Eligible For Overtime) This position is generally classified as exempt unless a non-exempt classification is required by applicable state law.
  • Purdue Global is an EO/EA employer. Our goal is to recruit and retain talent from a broad pool of applicants. Purdue Global celebrates a variety of perspectives, experiences, and skills to support a success-focused environment for employees and students. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs. All are encouraged to apply.

jobs.description:
About the Role

We are a fast-growing functional beverage brand selling across Australia, New Zealand, and the US through retail, eCommerce, and Amazon. We run three entities across three markets and are building a finance function with the rigour to match our growth.

You'll own day-to-day bookkeeping and accounting across all three entities, working closely with our fractional CFO and leadership team to keep the books accurate, timely, and audit-ready. Around 70–80% of the role is bookkeeping and reconciliations — the rest is month-end close, reporting prep, and building better systems and processes.

Work Structure & Requirements

Location: Remote / Virtual (Philippines)

Schedule: Full-time

Time Zone: AEST / AEDT (Australian Eastern Time)

Compensation: 10 USD per hour

Key Responsibilities

1. Bookkeeping & Reconciliations

Run day-to-day bookkeeping in Xero across AU, NZ, and US entities — coding, bank and card reconciliations, clearing suspense

Handle intercompany transactions and reconciliations, and multi-currency/FX entries

Reconcile eCommerce and marketplace payouts (Shopify, Amazon, payment gateways) back to sales, fees, and refunds

Support inventory and COGS reconciliations using stock reports from 3PLs and manufacturers

2. Accounts Payable & Receivable

Process and code supplier bills, prepare payment runs for approval, and keep supplier records current

Raise invoices, apply payments, chase overdue debtors, and reconcile retailer and distributor remittances and deductions

3. Month-End Close & Reporting

Deliver month-end close (accruals, prepayments, balance sheet reconciliations) to an agreed checklist and timetable for CFO review

Build and maintain finance trackers and reconciliations in Google Sheets

Keep receipts, documentation, and audit trails organised

4. Tax & Compliance Support

Prepare GST/BAS (AU), GST (NZ), and US sales tax workpapers

Work with external accountants in each country on tax lodgements and year-end

Document and improve finance processes, controls, and workflows

Required Skills & Experience

Xero Proficiency: Advanced Xero skills required — multi-entity and multi-currency experience is a strong plus

Accounting Experience: 3+ years of hands-on bookkeeping or accounting experience, ideally supporting Australian, NZ, or US clients

Qualifications: Degree in Accounting or Finance; CPA, CA, or ACCA qualified or part-qualified preferred

Spreadsheets: Strong Google Sheets skills including lookups, pivot tables, and building clean reconciliations

Industry: Experience in FMCG, eCommerce, or product businesses with inventory strongly preferred

Attention to Detail: Strong habit of reconciling everything — accuracy is non-negotiable in this role

Communication: Clear written and spoken English; confidence working directly with an Australian team and external advisers

Availability: Able to work full Sydney business hours (AEST/AEDT)

Nice to Have

Experience with A2X, Shopify, or Amazon Seller Central

Familiarity with inventory or 3PL systems

Exposure to US sales tax or multi-state compliance

jobs.description:
About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Staff Accountant to join our growing accounting team. This is a hands-on role for someone with a strong technical accounting foundation who enjoys solving problems, working across multiple client accounts, and delivering accurate, timely financial information.

This person will report directly to an Accounting Manager and work closely with the accounting team to support day-to-day client needs. The role combines traditional bookkeeping responsibilities with more technical accounting work, including monthly close, journal entries, reconciliations, and troubleshooting accounting issues.

Key Responsibilities

  • Perform day-to-day accounting and bookkeeping across multiple client accounts.
  • Categorize and record transactions in QuickBooks Online and other cloud-based accounting systems.
  • Perform bank, credit card, balance sheet, and other account reconciliations.
  • Support monthly close processes and preparation of accurate financial statements.
  • Prepare and post journal entries, including accruals, depreciation, payroll adjustments, and other necessary entries.
  • Research, troubleshoot, and resolve accounting discrepancies and client-specific accounting issues.
  • Maintain accurate, organized financial records and support cleanup or historical accounting projects as needed.
  • Gather financial information and documentation for tax, advisory, and other client needs.
  • Communicate proactively with Accounting Managers and other team members to resolve questions, obtain missing information, and keep client work moving.
  • Manage multiple client accounts, priorities, and deadlines with a high level of accuracy and follow-through.
  • Assist with process documentation and improvements to accounting workflows and internal systems.
  • Take on additional accounting responsibilities and projects as directed by the Accounting Manager.

What We're Looking For

The ideal candidate will bring:

  • A bachelor's degree in Accounting preferred. An associate degree or significant relevant accounting experience may be considered instead of a bachelor's degree.
  • Approximately 3–5 years of relevant accounting experience.
  • Strong understanding of accrual accounting and monthly close processes.
  • Proficiency with QuickBooks Online and comfort learning other cloud-based accounting platforms.
  • Ability to independently investigate and solve accounting problems rather than simply process transactions.
  • Strong reconciliation and journal-entry experience.
  • Excellent organization and attention to detail.
  • Ability to confidently manage multiple clients, priorities, and deadlines.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Comfort working independently in a fully remote environment while remaining highly collaborative with the team.
  • A proactive, solutions-oriented, team-first mindset.

Experience with multi-entity businesses, sales tax compliance, certified payroll, insurance retainage, or other accounting platforms is a plus.

Schedule & Location

This is a fully remote position working 32–40 hours per week.

Compensation

$70,000–$80,000 annually based on a 40-hour workweek

Benefits & Perks

  • Healthcare stipend: Up to $450/month for full-time employees, with a partial stipend available for employees working between 24 and 40 hours per week. Kingdom CFO does not currently offer group health insurance.
  • Employer-paid short- and long-term disability insurance for employees working more than 30 hours per week, effective on the employee's hire date.
  • 401(k) retirement plan through Human Interest, available to all employees; there is currently no employer match.
  • Paid time off: 10 days annually for employees with 0–5 years of service and 15 days after 5 years, plus five fixed office-closure days.
  • Paid holidays, including New Year's Day, MLK Day, Good Friday, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving and the day after, Christmas Eve, and Christmas Day, along with additional fixed office-closure days that typically create a full week off around Christmas.
  • $50/month remote-work reimbursement for home internet expenses.
  • Company-provided hardware and software needed to perform the role.
  • Professional development support, including approved courses, workshops, seminars, conferences, and other relevant training opportunities.
  • Certification reimbursement for eligible full-time employees with prior management approval.
  • Flexible work hours that allow employees to manage personal needs while remaining responsive to clients and the team.
Salary: 70,000-80,000

Anything is possible when you imagine everything.

Role Impact

Remote / Multi-Site – North America (Travel Required)

Alternate Titles: Network Reliability Engineer | Plant Reliability Engineer | Maintenance & Reliability Engineer

The Reliability Engineer is an individual contributor on a centralized reliability team supporting a network of small manufacturing plants across North America. This role drives the transition from reactive maintenance to a proactive, data-driven reliability culture by leading bad actor elimination, root cause analysis, and preventive/predictive maintenance improvement across multiple sites.

This position directly contributes to reduced unplanned downtime and improved asset performance by identifying the top failure drivers at each site, facilitating root cause analysis, and embedding sustainable reliability practices into the maintenance work management process. The Reliability Engineer serves as a key point of technical leadership and cross-site learning — replicating proven solutions across the plant network to prevent recurring failures and closing the loop between reliability data and executed work.

What You Will Do

Drive Bad Actor Elimination & Downtime Reduction

  • Pull and review downtime, failure, and repeat-work data from each site to identify the top 3–5 bad actors by highest loss or repeat failure
  • Focus reliability efforts on the largest sources of unplanned downtime, transitioning sites from reactive to controlled, planned maintenance
  • Monitor the effectiveness of corrective actions and system modifications to confirm sustained reliability improvement

Lead Asset Criticality Assessment & Ranking

  • Establish and maintain an asset criticality register across the plant network, ranking equipment by the safety, environmental, operational, and financial consequences of failure
  • Facilitate cross-functional criticality workshops with site operations, maintenance, and HSE to calibrate rankings and ensure a consistent, defensible standard across all sites
  • Use criticality rankings to prioritize maintenance strategy, PM coverage, spare parts stocking, and bad actor focus — directing limited central resources to the highest-consequence assets first
  • Periodically review and update criticality rankings as equipment, processes, and failure data change

Lead Root Cause Analysis & Failure Elimination

  • Lead or facilitate lightweight root cause analysis (RCA) for top bad actors and recurring failures
  • Determine the failure mode — design, operation, maintenance practice, or PM gap — and develop lasting corrective actions
  • Conduct Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) to proactively identify and mitigate potential equipment failures before they occur

Develop Preventive & Predictive Maintenance Strategies

  • Audit PM compliance and lubrication routes per site; flag gaps and update PM frequencies based on failure data
  • Lead lubrication excellence initiatives including lubrication strategy development, route optimization, contamination control, lubricant selection, storage and handling standards, lubrication PM optimization, and lubrication KPI tracking.
  • Apply predictive and condition-based maintenance techniques (e.g., vibration analysis, thermal imaging, ultrasonic testing) to anticipate failures and extend asset life
  • Apply Reliability-Centered Maintenance (RCM) principles to determine the optimal maintenance strategy for critical assets

Translate Reliability Actions into Executable Work

  • Assign corrective actions to the Site Reliability Owner or Local Work Owner and enter PM changes and job plan updates into the CMMS
  • Feed bad actor corrective actions into the weekly scheduling backlog to close the loop from data to execution
  • Maintain reliability data quality in the CMMS — asset hierarchy, failure codes, and work-order history — so criticality, bad actor, and KPI analysis rest on accurate data
  • Participate in weekly planning and scheduling reviews to ensure reliability actions, bad actor corrective work, PM improvements, and failure elimination activities are properly prioritized, planned, and scheduled for execution.

Drive Cross-Site Learning & Standardization

  • Share repeat failure patterns across the plant network and replicate proven solutions to prevent recurrence at other sites
  • Apply reliability engineering principles and best practices consistently across sites, projects, and processes
  • Support standardization of reliability processes, tools, and the monthly reliability cadence across the network

Build Site Reliability Capability & Culture

  • Train and coach Site Reliability Owners, Local Work Owners, and technicians on reliability fundamentals — defect identification, basic equipment care, and quality failure reporting — building lasting capability at each site
  • Champion the shift from reactive to proactive reliability, reinforcing planned-over-reactive work and data-driven decision-making across the network
  • Promote operator-driven reliability and basic-care routines so frontline teams catch early warning signs before they become failures

Track Performance & Report Results

  • Monitor key reliability KPIs — Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF), Mean Time To Repair (MTTR), asset availability, planned vs. reactive work ratio, and repeat failure rate per site
  • Apply statistical and life-data analysis (e.g., Pareto and Weibull) to quantify failure risk, set maintenance intervals, and prioritize improvement effort
  • Report reliability trends and improvement results to Maintenance Managers and Corporate Leadership
  • Establish and maintain data and records for tracking performance failures and improvement measures

Support Asset Lifecycle & Continuous Improvement

  • Support asset lifecycle management and life-cycle cost analysis to guide repair, replace, or redesign decisions
  • Analyze maintenance data to optimize spare parts inventory for critical components while controlling cost
  • Apply design-for-reliability principles to new installations and equipment modifications — setting reliability and maintainability specifications, supporting commissioning, and providing reliability input to the Management of Change (MOC) process
  • Ensure reliability activities align with site safety, environmental, and regulatory standards

What You Bring

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Industrial, or a related Engineering discipline (or equivalent technical experience)
  • Experience in reliability, maintenance, or engineering within an industrial or manufacturing environment
  • Working knowledge of reliability methodologies — root cause analysis (RCA), FMEA, and preventive and predictive maintenance
  • Experience using CMMS/EAM systems (e.g., SAP PM, Maximo, Infor)
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret failure and downtime data
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills to work effectively across multiple sites and functions
  • Willingness to travel across the plant network as required

Preferred Qualifications

  • Certified Maintenance & Reliability Professional (CMRP) or Certified Reliability Engineer (CRE) certification
  • Experience with predictive/condition-monitoring technologies (vibration analysis, thermal imaging, ultrasonic testing) and lubrication programs
  • Familiarity with Reliability-Centered Maintenance (RCM) and Total Productive Maintenance (TPM)
  • Experience performing asset criticality assessments and risk-based prioritization
  • Experience supporting multiple sites or a multi-plant network
  • Proficiency with statistical analysis tools and reliability KPIs (MTBF, planned vs. reactive ratio, repeat failure rate)
  • Experience leading cross-functional reliability or continuous improvement initiatives
  • Experience developing training or capability-building programs for site maintenance and operations teams
  • Familiarity with process safety management (PSM) and mechanical integrity requirements in a chemical or process manufacturing environment

Legal & Employment Notices

  • La maîtrise de l'anglais est un plus apprécié.
